Klotouch Editor is divided into four major sections, which are listed below.
The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

PageLayout is the topmost layer embedded with the page. At runtime, only one pageLayout will be picked based on the device type. The detail of which pageLayout needs to be picked is maintained in the page’s properties (screencontainerdefault, screencontainerdesktop, screencontainermobile, screenontainertab). If the property for a specific device type is not maintained then the default pageLayout will be rendered.

The Page area is the next level in the page hierarchy after the Page Layout. Page areas are embedded with the pagelayout. The detail of the page Area that needs to be rendered for the page area will be maintained in the Page Layout’s Layout Data section.

Sections are the building blocks of the pages. The page can have multiple sections, and the sections are embedded in a page Area. The detail of which section should be rendered for a page Area will be maintained in the page Area’s Layout data section.
Controls are used to define the appearance and behaviour parts of the section.

This is a screen that helps make changes in the settings and setting groups that are used in any application.

Note: If the developers want to make any changes to the Settings Definition Screen metadata then they will have to assign core_fw as a dependent app to the fw_settings1_1 app and then build the fw_settings1 flavor and reinitialize it. Only then any changes should be made. Also for save to work, assign is_external for fw_settings1 flavor as 1. To save any changes made on the Settings Definition user needs a shared, writable app.
Flavor: fw_settings1

Go to the menu App Settings. Click on the sub-menu named Settings Definition to open it. The Screen will be loaded initially with all the settings inside their respective Settings Group in a tree in ascending order based on their sequence value. Settings Group will also be in ascending order of their sequence values. Click on the Edit option in the upper right corner of the screen. On the toolbar of the screen, you will find the Create Group, Create Settings, Save, Delete and Cancel buttons. You can create the settings group by clicking the +Group button on the top right of the screen. It will ask the developer to provide the Settings Group ID in an input dialog. Click on the Create button in the input dialog. After creating a new Settings Group, users can see it updated in the Table Tree below. Users need to fill in the Sequence number, Title and Icon of that settings group and then click on the Save button to save the newly created settings group. All the settings groups will now be shown in ascending order of their sequence value. The developer then needs to create Settings inside the newly created settings group. To do that the user needs to select that settings group on the tree and then click on +Setting Button. It will ask for the Settings ID under Create Setting and the developer needs to provide the ID and click on the Create button. A new setting will be created inside the selected settings group. The developer needs to fill in the Title, Description, Sequence Number, Icon, Data Type, UI type, Vh ID, Default value, visible and modifiable_in and then click on Save to save all the changes. After successful save, all the settings in their respective groups will be in ascending order of their sequence value. Components Descriptions Title It's the name you want to put to identify the setting control. Description A short description of the setting element. Sequence Number This will put the setting elements according to the order of its sequence. Icon This implies an individual settings icon. Data Type It's the type of the setting, whether it's a number, an integer or a string etc. UI Type It is the type of Control that you want to render in the UI for those Settings such as Input, Slider, value Help, etc. Vh ID It is the value help ID created from bol editor on application flavor and it will be shown to the user as value help items in case the user has chosen UI type as VH. Default Value It's a pre-value that has been set for some particular setting. This is changeable according to your requirements. visible This implies who will be able to see the particular setting item. modifiable in This puts down conditions on who can see the setting items and so on. To update any details click on the edit button in the toolbar and after updating the details click on save to commit the changes. If you have updated any details and do not want it to commit then you can click on the reset button in the toolbar to set the details to the original state.

Expert Mode - It supports all the functionalities from the normal mode along with add-on features like Status Config, config properties for object type, and entity indexes. Note: One can switch between the two modes at any point in time.

Steps: Navigate to "Design Studio" -> "Data Studio" Screen and select your flavor. The flavor needs to be configured on the SAP side. The flavor_name and major_version should be the same. The minor version and patch version can be different from each other. Create a new entity and do not add any properties yet. Otherwise, use an existing entity having some existing properties. And then click the "Import from SAP" button. If the entity is maintained in the SAP-side, then it will show an error dialog. Else, the import process will start. Import from SAP on Existing Entity Data​ While doing import again on an existing entity having existing properties, it will ask the developer regarding the existing properties whether to keep those properties or delete them. Data Studio is divided into two major sections, which are listed below: Tree Detail
The tree present in the left section lists all the entities present in the selected app.
Expand All option is to expand all the collapsed sections (entity, query, value help).
Collapse all option is to collapse all the expanded sections (entity, query, value help)
This section contains all the details related to the selected entity/query or value help like properties, relations, object type, status, queries, and many more.

On selection of any entity in the tree, it will display all available options in the detail section. The description of each tab is given below: 2.2.1.1. Detail​ This section contains all the basic information about the entity. It contains fields like Root Entity name, App Mode, Entity Icon, Entity Name, Metadata type, and also a few buttons to enable or disable CRUD over the entity. The description of each field is provided below: BO/Root Entity :​ BO stands for Business Object. Root Entity means that if any entity is a root entity then it will have the same name as the BO and it will be the parent entity. App Mode :​ App mode refers to the network mode of the entity/query. It supports network modes such as those specified below: Offline :​ Offline network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. The application stores the relevant data locally and updates the local cache and server data as and when it finds connectivity. Browsers and installed mobile apps (client) both are capable of offline operations. In offline mode, the values are maintained/fetched from the web SQL. Online :​ Online network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) to communicate with the server for day-to-day needs. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. All the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving. In the online mode, the values are maintained/fetched from the transactional database. SAP Online :​ This refers to the capability of all the transactions that go to SAP via the gateway server. In SAP online mode the values are maintained/fetched from the SAP server. SAP Preferred Online :​ Any transaction that takes place between your application goes through SAP to your web SQL. Entity Icon :​ This will associate the specified icon with the entity. Entity Name :​ Entity name refers to the actual name/id of the entity. Metadata type:​ Runtime entity: This is the default type of entity, where the table persists in the DB (unlike Transient Entities). The table is created in the Trans DB and CRUD operations can be performed on it. Config entity: This is the type of entity, where the table persists but only in meta DB. This is usually used to store data for status and role fields. Transient Entities​ A transient entity is a non-persistent entity---meaning it does not store data in the database. It is primarily used for runtime calculations, data aggregation, or displaying derived data in the UI. These entities are ideal when you need to display or process combined data from multiple sources without storing it permanently. Use Case Example: Suppose you have two entities and want to display certain fields from each, but do not wish to persist the combined data. In this case: Create a transient entity that includes only the required properties. Write custom logic to query both source entities. Populate the transient entity with the result. Display this transient data on the screen with full support for UI features like Sort, Filter, and Fuzzy Search. Users can also fetch data from external sources, populate the transient entity, and leverage built-in platform features such as:Sort, Filter, Fuzzy search, Excel download,Pivot view (report/chart generation). NOTE: Data Must Be Fully Loaded:The transient entity's query must execute with loadAll: true. Unique Primary Key: Ensure that the transient entity has a unique primary key to enable proper identification and UI support. Custom Data Handling Logic: You must define how and from where the data is fetched, processed, and whether or not it should be saved back to a persistent entity. Persists On :​ Persists On consists of three options which are explained below: null -​ Entities will be created based on the app's network mode. If the network mode of the app is online then it will be created on the server side. If the network mode of the app is offline then it will be created in web sql. Both -​ Entities will be created for both sides. Client Only -​ An entity will only be created in web SQL for the device or browser during registration. Server Only -​ An entity will be created in server-side DB and not in web SQL. NOTE: Entity persistence will be decided primarily based on the Persists On mentioned. In case the persist on is set as null , Persists On will be checked based on app network mode. Offline Flavor - Entity will be created in both server and client DB Online Flavor - Entity will be created only on server DB. Universal Link Details :​ Universal Link Details is used to build a Universal Link that opens the specific record of the current entity in its respective screen based on the provided parameters. These parameters are similar to navTo parameters available in screens which will be used for generating the deep link. Target Page -​ Screen Id of the page. Section -​ Section to which the link needs to be navigated. Page Data Model -​ Name of the transnode to which the link needs to be navigated. Query Parameters -​ Additional QueryParameters that need to be passed to the navigated screen. Create Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the creation accessibility over the entity. Read Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the data read access over the entity. Delete Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the deletion accessibility over the entity. Update Allowed:​ This button enables/disables the modification access over the entity. 2.2.1.2. Properties​ This tab contains all the properties present inside the entity. It is also used to add/delete properties from the entity. Entity Property is also known as an attribute or variable in an entity or field in the database table. The entity Detail section consists of multiple fields. All the fields are explained below : Entity Property ID :​ Property ID is unique within the entity across all apps. Once created this can't be changed later. PROC-27544: List of Reserved Keywords in Data Studio Application - List of reserved keywords which are not restricted to use as property ID value. Short Label :​ Provide label for your property which will be used as labels in screen. Note: It is recommended not to provide same label for two or more properties. Validation Warning: Key Attributes :​ Key attributes show whether the property is a primary key, mandatory, or auto-incrementing field. Each of these attributes is explained in the below table: Icon Description This icon shows if the respective property is a primary key or not. If it's highlighted, then it's a primary key, else not. Each entity should have a primary key irrespective of the entity type This icon shows whether the selected property is mandatory or not. If any property is marked as compulsory, its value needs to be maintained before saving it to the DB. If the icon is highlighted, the entity is compulsory. This icon represents whether the respective property has auto-incrementing functionality or not. This icon indicates whether the chosen property is a unique key. When highlighted, it means the selected property will only store unique data in the database. If a user attempts to add duplicate data, an error will occur. This icon indicates whether the selected property is a Parent key, meaning it is common to both the parent and child entities. A parent key is created only when a child entity exists, and all primary keys of the parent entity are established as parent keys in the child entity. Value Help :​ Can set the already defined value help for this property. Default Value :​ It refers to the predefined value for that specific property. This field will be automatically filled with the specified value. Qualifier :​ Add a Qualifier for the entity. A qualifier helps to make the entity property work in a predefined manner. The property with qualifier stores and acts as per the definition of the qualifier. Please refer to Qualifiers to know more about qualifiers. Root :​ Root key​ All primary properties of a Business Object (BO) will be designated as Root keys in its child entities. This can be identified by checking the property details and if the Root checkbox is true,it indicates that the property is a root key. On adding data using a data browser, it will copy the data of the Root Key from its immediate parent. NOTE 1: Root keys are created only when the child entity is created. NOTE 2: In the case of the Parent Child flavor scenario, the data type (domain, length, etc.) for the same Property Id in both the flavors should not be the same. Is Unique Key:​ A unique key can be assigned to any property, aside from the primary key. When a child entity is created, all the root and parent keys are automatically marked as unique, and an index is generated for them. Any regular property can be designated as a unique key. **Use Case of Unique Key: **Consider a student table that includes columns for registration number (reg_no), student name (student_name), and date of birth (date_of_birth), with multiple records where the reg_no is the primary key. reg_no(Primary) student_name date_of_birth 1001 Ankit 21/04/2001 1002 Abhijith 22/08/2005 1003 Amit 12/02/2004 1004 Prem 08/05/2000 ** **Consider adding a new column, "aadhar_no," to store the Aadhaar numbers of all the students. Since each Aadhaar number should be unique, we want to ensure the database doesn't allow duplicate entries. The only option available is to mark "aadhar_no" as a primary key, but this would prevent the user from making any updates to the existing data. To solve this, the concept of a unique key is introduced. By marking the "aadhar_no" as a unique key, we ensure that duplicate values can't be stored in the column while still allowing null values. This allows us to modify the data in the table without enforcing a primary key constraint. reg_no(Primary) student_name aadhar_no(unique) date_of_birth 1001 Ankit 21/04/2001 1002 Abhijith 22071 22/08/2005 1003 Amit 12/02/2004 1004 Prem 08/05/2000 When a property is marked as unique, it offers the following benefits: It prevents the storage of duplicate data, regardless of case (case-insensitive). It allows null values to be stored in the column. When creating a child entity, it is mandatory to mark a property as unique to support the "one parent, multiple children" concept. This is because the parent key, which is unique, will be fetched from the parent entity and referenced in the child. If someone tries to add another child with the same parent data, a unique key violation will occur. To resolve this, an additional unique key must be defined in the child entity that is independent of the parent entity. When a unique key is defined in a child entity that has a primary relationship with a parent entity, uniqueness is enforced as a composite constraint comprising the parent key and the child unique key (i.e., parent_key + unique_key). Is Parent Key:​ All the primary properties of the immediate parent entity will be created as Parent Key in the child entity and will be marked as regular. This property cannot be changed by the user. On adding data from Data Browser, it will copy the Parent Key data from its parent and create it in the child. Formula:​ It is a property of an entity. It evaluates the given expression and returns the evaluated result. Example : Syntax : ={"test "+ this.order_id } Here this.order_id is the entity property Data Type:​ It is a property data type. Ex- String, Boolean, Integer.Data type conversion in the Data Studio is only available for compatible data types, as outlined in the provided Excel file;Data Type Conversion. Filter Option:​ If this field is marked as true for a property then only applyFilterP API can be used for that property. Is Restricted:​ If this field is marked as true for a property which has a value help assigned to it then validation will be called for this property in UI which will check if the key is present in the value help. Min Value:​ The minimum value is the minimum value for your property that a user can enter. Max Value:​ The maximum value is the maximum value for your property that a user can enter. Authorization:​ The authorization field takes the Login user id as an input and only that user can get access to that property. Ex- $USER.login_id ID Series : ID series is used for populating the IDs/Keys in the entity's property with kloBO. If an application wants to allocate the ID itself, either it should not assign the ID series or mark it as none. kloBO will allocate the ID on the first read of the ID. Transient Property:​ An entity property can be made transient by setting the type of property to "Transient Field" so that within that entity property's value is not stored in the database. It exists only at runtime and is never persisted in or retrieved from the database. Use Cases: **Accessing Properties of Relational Entities ** Transient fields can be used to display values from related entities without actually adding them as properties/database table columns. For example, if an entity is related to another entity(e.g., User → Department), a transient field like departmentName can fetch and show department.name without requiring an actual field in the database. **Custom Getter/Setter Logic **Standard transient property getters and setters can be used for dynamically calculating values, formatting data before sending it in a response, or temporarily accepting input and storing it without saving it to the database. In this example, d_customer is the entity, and fullName is a transient property. The fullName property is computed from the underlying firstName and lastName fields. The getter and setter for fullName should be written directly inside the entity file /src/<app folder>/entity/d_customer.ts Eg: get fullName(): string { return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`; } set fullName(name: string) { const [firstName, lastName] = name.split(' '); this.firstName = firstName; this.lastName = lastName; } Note : In case a user wants to change the property type of any property, they have to re-add the same property in their screen metadata using UI Editor (wherever applicable) from their transnode for reflecting the changes. For ex: This is the property type created by default using Data Studio: Suppose the property type has been changed as per below: To reflect the same changes in the application as well please follow the mentioned steps: Step 1: Open the screen metadata in the UI Editor. Now delete all occurrences of the changed property type's property. Step 2: Now drag and drop the same property from the transnode to the section. Created By / Modified By Value Help:​ The system fields s_created_by and s_modified_by store the user ID of the user who created or last changed a record. These fields have a built-in value help, so screens and data views show the user's name instead of the login ID. Features: Names instead of user IDs: the user's display name is shown wherever these fields appear. Filter and search: filtering and fuzzy search work on the user's name. Sorting: the columns sort by the user's name. NOTE: Created By is fixed: once a record is saved, s_created_by can't be changed. Any attempt to change it is ignored. Modified By is automatic: s_modified_by is updated every time the record is saved. 2.2.1.3. Relations​ This tab contains all the relations created inside the entity. Entity relation relates one entity with another entity. Entity relation consists of multiple fields. All the fields are explained below: Relation Type:​ It specifies the type of the relation whether it's a primary or non-primary relation. This also contains two icons which are described below: Primary Relation​ Primary relation is a special kind of aggregate relation within the BO boundary. All entities in a BO are navigable from the root entity only once unidirectional. A primary relation is a direct relation between two entities. There will be a parent entity and a child entity and the child entity will be dependent on the parent entity. The Return Entity value help is applicable only for aggregate (non-primary) relations. The primary relation is created only during the creation of a child entity and cannot be assigned by selecting a return entity. Aggregated Relation​ An aggregation relationship can be described in simple words as "an object of one class can own or access the objects of another class". If a parent is deleted/archived, all other parts associated with it are deleted. Aggregated relations can be across BOs. When a relation is created as non-primary, the related data cannot be fetched in callbacks if both the parent and child entities are being saved in the same transaction. This occurs because the child entity has not yet been persisted at the time the relation is evaluated, and therefore the relation data is unavailable. Icon Description This shows whether a relation is primary or not. This icon displays whether a relation is aggregated or not. Relation Name:​ Unique within an Entity. Relation names and Property names can't be the same. Description:​ Provides a small description of the relation. Return Entity:​ Return entity is the actual name of the entity. Relation Query:​ The relation Query is the entity/query ID using which the relation needs to be established. NOTE: If the relation is created using a relation query, the relational data will be fetched according to that query. Therefore, features like sort order should be implemented at the query level, rather than at the entity level, to retrieve the data in the correct sorted order. Cardinality:​ Cardinality shows how the entities are connected. Select the cardinality for the relation (0:n, 1:1, 1:n). 0:n - Zero to Many relationships (A minimum cardinality of 0 indicates that the relationship is optional.) 1:1 - One to One relationship 1:n - One to Many relationships Mapping:​ It will map based on the target entity property and source entity property with a mapping type. This field provides the following options: ON CREATE ( mapping will be called On Create of an entity) ON QUERY ( mapping will be called On execution of an entity query) BOTH Note:​ In case of aggregated relation where the mapping property of the entity is null, then all the data of the related entity will be fetched from the relation 2.2.1.4. Object Type​ Object Type defines the possible behaviour of an entity / BO. Object type has a unique key and description. Object type contains multiple fields which are explained below: Object Type:​ This field displays the object type. The object type may include alphabets or numerals. Object Group:​ It is a group of object types. Select the object group from the drop-down. 2.2.1.5. Status​ This tab is used for the configuration and maintenance of status-based data under specified object types. This also helps in assigning status, and status groups under specific object types. This tab consists of a few fields which are mentioned below. Object Type:​ This field displays the object types available for this entity. The object type may include alphabets or numerals. Icon:​ This field displays an icon for your newly created entry in the status section. Description:​ A short description Status:​ This field displays the entity status which you are going to map with the status group Status Group: This field lists down the predefined status groups, which can be mapped with the status and will be used in Vienable. NOTE: If changing any system field property's (s_status, s_object_type, s_status_group) propertytype columns, will change it in the whole app. For ex: If changing the value help id of s_status property from "vh_s_status" to "vhc_city" then this change will reflect in each of the entities s_status property wherever added. 2.2.1.6. Queries​ This tab will list all the queries present under the current entity. Using this section we can also add new queries. Queries consist of a few fields like Query ID and description. Query ID:​ The query ID is the name of the query which is used to identify the specific query. Description:​ A short description of the query. 2.2.1.7. Entity Index​ The Entity index tab is used to retrieve data from a database very fast. When you are creating indexing, It will create an index in your database along with the properties you have added. Next time when you search those properties, It will directly fetch that index from the database and give you the data. An index on a table works like an index in a book (that's where the name came from): Let's say you have a book about databases and want to find some information about storage. Without an index (assuming no other aid, such as a table of contents) you'd have to go through the pages one by one until you found the topic (that's a full table scan). On the other hand, an index has a list of keywords, so you'd consult the index and see that storage is mentioned on pages 113-120,231 and 354. Then you could flip to those pages directly, without searching (that's a search with an index, somewhat faster). Entity Index creation: Step 1: Go to the Entity Index tab and click on the add icon(+) Entity index consists of a few fields which are mentioned below: ID: The entity index ID is used to identify the specific entity index. Description: A short description of the entity index. Properties: Properties for your indexing. These properties data will be retrieved very fast. Client/Server: Entity indexing will call on which side, server-side, client-side or both. Step 2: Fill in the detail section as per your requirement. Step 3: Click on the save button. NOTE: Indices will be created based on the Client/Server mentioned. Server Only - Creates index only in server DB Client Only - Creates only in client/local DB Both - Creates on both server and client Deletion of Entity Indexes is supported at both entity level and flavor level update schema , but some points have to be kept under consideration. In a parent-child scenario, if an index is deleted from the parent but still exists in the child, triggering an update schema on the child entity will cause the index to be added back. To avoid inconsistencies, an index must be deleted from both the parent and child entities. 2.2.1.8. Rules​ A Rule is a program containing business logic written by a Developer as per the application's needs. It works with the event bus, any change in entity triggers the event, and all the rules hooked to the event bus are executed sequentially. Rules are reusable objects across client, server, and middleware. Rules are reusable and hence can be subscribed multiple times with different Channel types or other combinations. Entity Rule Creation:​ Step 1: Go to the Rule tab and click on the add icon(+). Field Description Event type Select the event type. Based on the type of event you choose rule will be executed. Type Select the channel type, based on this the transaction will be performed. Exit ID is an ID you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Clazz This will be the rule file name. Invocation Method The method needs to be called. Step 2: Select the Event Type from the drop-down. The event type will mention when the rules will be executed. Event types: Endpoint resolver (Once the rule is being executed in-between it picks Endpoint Resolver and resolves it or whenever the online save is going to the klarion server Endpoint resolver will get called) On Create ( rule will be executed on create of an entity) On Delete (rule will be executed on delete of an entity) On Update (rule will be executed on update of an entity) Step 3: Select the channel type(there are different input channels to perform a transaction on an entity, channel type selection decides when to trigger the Rule). Channel Type: Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on the client Endpoint / Device on Klarion server Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on server Endpoint / Device to Server/ Client -Network Context Switch Legacy on Klarion server Klarion server to Klarion offline server Klarion server to Klarion Server Step 4: Fill in the value for Exit ID. Exit ID: It's an ID that you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Step 5: In the Clazz field provide the rule file name (example: rules/<file_name>) and in the invocation method provide an event name. You will be using that event to write your business logic codes. NOTE: If you are creating a Rule for the same entity you can fill this inside the Clazz field. Step 6: Click on the save button to save the newly created rule. Note: The last column drop-down icon has two fields(Choose Existing and Create New) Choose Existing: This will list down all the existing rules for that entity. You directly select it and use it. Create New: Create New will clear some fields from the created rule fields. For more information, please refer to the training guide. Debugging a Legacy to Klarion Server Callback on a Private Node:​ A Legacy to Klarion Server (E2K_MSG) rule runs when a legacy system, such as SAP, sends a message to the Klarion application. These messages are processed on the server nodes, so the rule can't normally be debugged from a private node. To debug such a rule, the node ID of the private node should be sent in the message header. The message is then processed on that private node, where breakpoints can be used like for any other rule. Steps: Start the private node and note its node ID. Send the message with the header nodeid set to the node ID of the private node. The private node picks up the message and runs the Legacy to Klarion Server (E2K_MSG) rule. Debug the rule from the debugger attached to the private node. NOTE: If the header is not sent, the message is processed on the server nodes as usual.

On selection of any query in the tree, it will display all available options in the detail section. The description of each tab is given below: 2.2.2.1. Detail​ This tab will list all the basic information related to the query. It contains fields like return entity, DB Selection, Select distinct, app mode, Tenant level, query type and expand all. The description of each of the fields is given below: Return Entity:​ Return entity indicates the return type of the query. The second field of the return entity is the Alias of that entity. Transient Entity (Aggregate Queries)​ In the case of aggregate queries and native aggregate queries, an additional field called Transient Entity is present. In the UI Editor, Page Data Model will be created from the Transient Entity rather than the return entity. The Transient Entity will include all the properties from the SELECT clause, ensuring that all values are properly displayed on the screen. Differences Between Aggregate and Native Aggregate Queries Aggregate query automatically generates a transient entity containing all properties used in the SELECT clause. If no SELECT clause is modeled, the return entity is used instead. Properties added automatically by the framework to the transient entity cannot be deleted. However, users can add their own properties to the transient entity for additional calculations, display purposes, or other operations. Native aggregate queries require the user to explicitly create a transient entity and assign it to the "Transient Entity" in the detail tab of the query. All aliases must be included as properties; if no alias is provided, the property name from the Entity should be included in the query. Note: For native aggregate queries, if a transient entity is not specified manually, it will be defaulted to the return entity. DB Selection:​ We have two DB instances, one is Reader and another is Writer, where Writer is RunTimeMain and Reader is RunTimeSecondary. We can shift the load of a particular query to the Reader instance by maintaining the proper DB Selection. By default it runs on RunTimeMain. In case of RunTimeSecondary, if we are updating some property of the entityset it will persist via RunTimeMain. Select Distinct:​ This field specifies whether the query created will be giving unique records or not. Select Distinct returns unique records based on the specified columns. If the selected columns are not primary keys, and loadAll is false, the distinction is made based on the primary key, which might still include duplicates. To ensure distinctness based on the selected columns, loadAll must be set to true. App Mode:​ App mode refers to the network mode of the entity. This is similar to what we get in identity-level app mode. Click here to read about supported app modes in detail. Tenant Level:​ This radio button allows you to make the dependent or independent. Query Type:​ Query supports multiple types of query modelling which are easy to define and use in the application. Based on the application scenario and use case, the query type has to be decided. Runtime Query ( former Entity Query)​ Modelled Query (former Dynamic Query)​ Native Query (former Advanced Query)​ Aggregate Query (ReadOnly with Modelling support)​ Native Aggregate Query (ReadOnly with Raw SQl)​ Note: Changing modelled query to aggregate/native aggregate will trigger a dialog mentioning the warnings which have to resolved depending on the developer's need. On click of Open Where Used List, a dialog will appear mentioning if any screen is created using the query. Query Modelling​ Update:​ This will update the SQL query generated as per the data maintained for the query. Expand All:​ The "Expand All" text area contains all the relations for which the data will be loaded during the parent query execution.Currently, ExpandAll does not work when an INNER JOIN is used in a query, as we do not support the combination of ExpandAll and INNER JOIN together. Note: Expand All is not supported for aggregate queries. When a query uses aggregate functions (like SUM, COUNT, AVG, etc.), it consolidates multiple rows into summary values. Because of this aggregation, the original row-level detail is lost. Expand All relies on accessing these underlying row-level relations to fetch related data. Since the individual rows no longer exist in the aggregated result, it is not possible to expand relations in this context. Expand All with Joins: The Expand All feature is supported in queries that include joins. Joins defined in the parent query are automatically appended during Expand All execution. Entity Restrictions: The same entity cannot be used simultaneously in both the main query and in the Expand All clause. This restriction helps avoid circular references and data redundancy. Where Conditions on Joined Entities: You can apply WHERE conditions on secondary (joined) entities in queries that use Expand All. This is considered while filtering of expanded data. Note:Supported Functionality (BOL_ Version 7-2-113 and onwards) 2.2.2.2. Entities And Join​ In this tab, we can manually add the joins and choose join types. We can also manually select the fields and can group/order the fields. In the Entity Join section of our queries, we can now incorporate fixed values such as 100, 200, 'RAM', 'Rincy', 'Karan', as well as system variables like $SYSTEM.userID and $SYSTEM.now within the join conditions. Note:To ensure uniqueness in the results, we enable the SELECT DISTINCT option. Below are the details of the fields shown above in the image Entity:​ This field is for root entities. The entity to which we are applying the Joins. Description: A short description for entity join Join Type: A JOIN clause is used to combine rows from two or more tables. There are four types of join. 2.2.2.3. Select Properties​ This tab contains information about properties in the select clause. All the properties present in the query will be listed here. Unlike modeled queries, aggregate queries allow the same property to be included multiple times with different aggregation functions. For example: Counting the number of cities and also listing the names of the cities. Calculating the minimum, maximum, and average values of a property such as marks. Note: Each aggregated instance of a property must have a unique alias to ensure that all values are displayed correctly in the query result. All the fields of this screen are described below: Entity​ Entity name of the selected property. Property​ Entity property ID which is present in the query. Description​ A short description of the query. Key Attributes​ This field represents whether the respective property is primary, mandatory, or has an id-series or not. Click here to learn more about each of these. Alias​ Alias refers to the SQL aliases used to give a table, or a column in a table, a temporary name. Aggregation​ Aggregation in a query refers to the process of combining multiple rows of data into a single summary value. It is commonly used to calculate metrics such as sum, average, count, maximum, minimum, or other summary statistics. Note: When using a modeled query, it is recommended to provide an alias to display the aggregated value on the screen. This can be done either by creating a transient property or by using an existing property. Or the count_of_property or other aggregated result returned by the database may not appear in the transient node or returned entity. Additional Note: When performing aggregation within an aggregate query, an alias is automatically generated. However, it can also be manually specified if desired. 2.2.2.4. Parameters​ This tab lists all the query properties that are created under this query. A query property is similar to what an entity is having but this property will be used only in the runtime and no actual attributes will be added in the database table. Below is the definition of the fields shown above in the image: Query Property ID:​ Provide the ID for query property (should only contain small chars, numerical, '_'). This is the unique key used for accessing the specified query property. Short Label:​ Mention the label which is required to be shown in the UI when using search or any other function. Default Value:​ When providing default value in a query property it will act as a predefined value for that property and when the query will be executed it will prefill the query property with the provided default value. Description: A short description of the query property. Property Type:​ Property Type is generated in association with the query ID. This also refers to the element ID. Domain:​ It shows the data type for the query property. This generally means what will be the data type of the property specified like String, Int, Boolean, etc. Length:​ This field will display the length of the field specified. For example: For String it can have a Length 255 or 32; For Integer it can have a length of 16,32 or 64 etc. 2.2.2.5. Where​ Where the tab contains all the conditional data present in the query. To use the where clause, follow these steps: Step 1: Go to the Where tab and click on Add icon(+) Step 2: Fill the fields according to your requirements. Step 3: Click on save button 2.2.2.6. Group By​ Group by tab contains all the properties present in the group by clause. To use a group, follow these steps: Step 1: Go to group by tab and click on add icon(+) Step 2: Select the field from vh on which you want to apply group by Step 3: Click on the save button 2.2.2.7. Having​ The Having tab will list down all the properties present in the having clause. To use having on an entity property follow the same steps as we followed in the Where clause 2.2.2.8. Sort Order​ Sort order is used to sort the property in either ascending or descending order. The fields are explained below: Field:​ It refers to the property for which a sort order has been created. Order:​ Order specifies whether the data will be sorted in ascending or descending order. Note: To use sort order on any property, go to the sort order tab and inside that tab click on the add icon(+) fill in the data for your requirement and click on the save button. 2.2.2.9. Expand All​ The "Expand All" tab contains all the relations in one place for which the data will be loaded during the parent query execution. Note: In all the above sections listed, you can add and delete properties as and when required. The option for the same is given in all the sections.

VH_TRANSACTION​ VH Transaction is a common ValueHelp functionality provided by KloBase which can fulfil most of the basic requirements in the application. The rest of the entities (child entities) are aggregated into root entities to construct the entity tree. The root entity represents the BO, root entity name becomes the BO name. Root entity also takes full responsibility as BO apart from its entity responsibility.

If a property's type or attributes (e.g. precision, length) were changed in the metadata since the table was last created, clicking Update Schema may show a confirmation dialog listing the incompatible changes, for example: Some incompatible changes were found. Please press OK if you want to make the changes forcefully. NOTE: This will change / truncate the data in the table. followed by one line per affected property, e.g. Incompatible changes found (DEC:-decimal -> DEC:-decimal) in property:<property_name> in entity:<entity_name> in flavor:<flavor_name>. This means the metadata definition and the physical database column are out of sync --- usually because a prior property change (e.g. a precision or type change) was saved in metadata but Update Schema was not confirmed at that time. Clicking OK applies the change to the table forcefully. Existing data in the affected column(s) may be truncated or altered --- for example, reducing decimal precision will truncate any stored values beyond the new precision. Confirm this is acceptable, or back up/migrate the affected data first, before proceeding. Clicking Cancel leaves the table unchanged. The metadata will continue to report the new definition (e.g. the new precision) even though the underlying table still uses the old one --- this mismatch is silent and will resurface anywhere the discrepancy matters (e.g. UI display of decimal precision) until Update Schema is confirmed. Recommendation: Always confirm Update Schema in the same session as a property type/precision change, so metadata and the physical schema never drift apart.

kloQuery is a metamodel for fetching the data from the data store, like SQL in RDBMS. For example, the entity (table) name "d_order" has multiple columns including "s_status". To fetch all the records for open order in RDBMS need SQL as "Select ord_id, qty, ord_date from d_order WHERE d_order.status = 'open' Orderby ord_date ASC" and execute to get the desired result. kloQuery behaves similarly with a few value-added services, it gives the ability to fetch the data seamlessly for both offline and online applications. Abstracts out multiple syntaxes of Odata, SQL, JSON, etc. so that programmers can concentrate on the business logic. It gives a few short-hand optimizations like pagination column selection. Security features like authorization etc.

Row wise authorization is a security feature provided by a framework with which access to entity data can be restricted to selective row items on user level. By default, when a simple select query is fired on any entity, it returns all data that is present in the entity. But, by enabling and configuring row wise authorization on an entity, the list of records accessible to any user can be controlled using access tokens.

Step 1: Enable the Row Wise Authorization flag. Step 2: Click on add button which will create a new line item. Step 3: Fill the id which is the primary key, access key and then click on the property column icon to add properties. Developer AI is an enhancement to the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform that enables users to build enterprise applications by describing their requirements in natural language. Instead of manually configuring application components, users can generate applications through a single prompt, significantly accelerating the application development process.

Developer AI is an AI-powered application development capability built on top of the Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform. It transforms business requirements, provided in natural language, into a structured application design and automatically generates the foundational components required to build an enterprise application. Rather than requiring users to manually analyze requirements, design data models, create user interfaces, and configure application components, Developer AI automates these activities using artificial intelligence. This significantly reduces the time and effort involved in the initial stages of application development while ensuring consistency and alignment with business requirements.

When a user provides a business requirement through a prompt, Developer AI performs the following activities: Requirement Understanding Interprets the user's business requirement using Natural Language Processing (NLP). Identifies the business objective, workflows, business entities, users, and relationships. Extracts key functional and data requirements from the provided description. Business Analysis Converts the natural language requirement into structured business insights. Identifies business processes, modules, and system interactions. Determines the application's functional scope and required components. Data Model Generation Analyzes the business entities involved. Identifies attributes, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships. Generates a normalized data model suitable for the application. Diagram Generation Based on the analyzed requirements, Developer AI automatically generates design artifacts such as: Entity Relationship (ER) Diagram Data Relationship Diagrams Business Process Flow Diagrams Other architecture and visualization diagrams required for application planning These diagrams provide a clear visual representation of the application's structure before development begins. Entity Creation Creates all required business entities. Defines fields, data types, validations, constraints, and relationships. Configures entities according to Procify platform standards. Screen Generation Developer AI automatically generates the application's user interface, including: Data Entry Screens List/Grid Views Detail Pages Forms Navigation structure The generated screens are mapped directly to the underlying business entities and workflows. Dashboard Generation Based on the application's business context, Developer AI creates dashboards containing: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Charts and Graphs Summary Cards Business Metrics Data Visualizations These dashboards provide users with meaningful insights into their business data from the outset. Application Foundation Creation After generating the business model, entities, screens, and dashboards, Developer AI produces the initial application structure within the Procify platform. This foundation serves as the starting point for further customization, refinement, and deployment.

Developer AI is designed to simplify and accelerate enterprise application development by leveraging Artificial Intelligence. It minimizes manual effort in the initial stages of development and enables organizations to transform business ideas into functional applications more efficiently.

Accelerates Application Development Converts business requirements into application components within minutes, significantly reducing development time. Reduces Manual Effort Eliminates the need for manually analyzing requirements, designing data models, and creating initial application structures. Converts Natural Language into Applications Enables users to describe business requirements in plain language, allowing AI to generate the application's foundation automatically. Automates Requirement Analysis Interprets business requirements and extracts key business entities, workflows, relationships, and functional requirements. Generates Design Artifacts Automatically Creates Entity Relationship (ER) diagrams, business process diagrams, and other visual models without manual intervention. Automatically Creates Business Entities Generates entities, attributes, relationships, validations, and data models based on the identified business requirements. Builds User Interface Components Automatically creates forms, screens, list pages, navigation, and dashboards, reducing UI development effort. Ensures Consistency and Standardization Produces applications following Procify platform standards and best practices, ensuring uniformity across projects. Improves Productivity Allows developers to focus on business logic and advanced customizations instead of repetitive setup tasks. Accelerates Time-to-Market Reduces the overall application development lifecycle, enabling organizations to deliver solutions faster. Minimizes Human Errors Automates repetitive design and configuration tasks, reducing the likelihood of manual mistakes. Supports Rapid Prototyping Enables quick creation of application prototypes that can be reviewed, refined, and enhanced based on stakeholder feedback. Enhances Collaboration Provides generated diagrams and structured application models that improve communication between business users, analysts, and developers. Scales with Business Needs Supports the rapid creation of applications of varying complexity while maintaining consistency and quality. Provides a Strong Application Foundation Generates the initial application structure, allowing developers to focus on enhancements, integrations, and business-specific customizations rather than starting from scratch.

documents.t: The Upload Business Requirement Document screen is the first step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this step, users select the target application, review the available AI token quota, and upload the Business Requirement Document (BRD) or Business Blueprint (BBP) that Developer AI will analyze to generate the application. Select Application​ The Select Application dropdown displays all applications, select application with Developer AI enabled the selected application acts as the target application where Developer AI will generate all the required components. All AI-generated artifacts, such as entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, and configurations, are created within the selected application. Ensure the correct application is selected before proceeding with document upload. Note :- 1. Developer AI not Enabled for Application If Developer AI is not enabled for the selected Application, It will show warning that Developer AI is not enabled for that application 2. Developer AI server is not available If the Developer AI Server is not running, a dialog will be displayed with the message: “Developer AI server is currently unavailable. Kindly contact the Administration team.” 3. BBP Build is triggered when other BBP build is in-progress in the same application If Build is triggered in the same application when other BBP Build is in-progress in the same application, then also the warning will come showing the BBP Build is already in progress Token Quota​ The Token Quota section displays the AI token consumption details for the selected user. A token represents a unit of text processed by the AI model. Every analysis performed on a BRD or BBP consumes tokens. The Token Quota panel provides the following information: Tokens Used – Total number of tokens consumed by Developer AI. Total Token Allocation – Maximum tokens allocated to the application. Remaining Tokens – Tokens still available for future AI operations. Usage Percentage – Visual progress bar showing the percentage of the allocated quota that has been consumed. Token Units​ Developer AI displays large token counts using abbreviated units: Unit Meaning Example K Thousand (1,000) 250K = 250,000 tokens M Million (1,000,000) 2.0M = 2,000,000 tokens Example If the Token Quota displays: 2.0M / 26.5M tokens 7% Used 24.5M Remaining It means: A total of 26.5 million tokens have been allocated. 2.0 million tokens have already been consumed. 24.5 million tokens are still available. Approximately 7% of the total token allocation has been utilized. Generate BBP​ The Generate BBP feature enables users to generate a Business Blueprint (BBP) by simply describing their application requirements in natural language. Instead of manually preparing a detailed BBP document, users can provide a high-level business description, and Developer AI automatically transforms it into a structured Business Blueprint. Upload BRD / BBP Document​ Once the application has been selected, upload the project documentation for analysis. Developer AI supports the following documents: Business Requirement Document (BRD) Business Blueprint (BBP) The document can be uploaded by: Dragging and dropping the file into the upload area. Selecting the file from the local system. Once the document is uploaded, Developer AI begins analyzing its contents to understand the business requirements and extract key information required to build the application. During this process, Developer AI identifies and generates: Business entities Functional requirements User roles Application screens Menu structure Business workflows Notifications Schedulers Dashboard requirements Homepage configuration Relationships between business objects The extracted information is then used to automatically generate the initial application structure within the selected Procify application. Preparing a BBP for Developer AI​ Developer AI expects the Business Blueprint (BBP) to follow a predefined structure for accurate analysis and application generation. If your existing BBP is not already in this format, it must be converted before uploading. To prepare a Developer AI-compatible BBP: Ensure you have the existing Business Blueprint (BBP) for your project. Refer to the Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt document (Prompt). Upload both: Your existing BBP. The Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt. Submit both documents to Claude for processing. The conversion prompt has been specifically designed and validated for Claude, and it is recommended not to use other AI models for this conversion. Claude will generate a new BBP that conforms to the standardized format required by Developer AI. Review the generated BBP to verify that the business requirements have been accurately converted. Upload the converted BBP using the Upload Business Requirement Document section to continue the application generation process. Once uploaded, Developer AI will analyze the standardized BBP and generate the application's foundational components, including entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, configurations, and other required artifacts.

documents.t: The Analyze & Review tab is the second step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this stage, Developer AI processes the uploaded BRD or BBP and extracts all the business information required to build the application. The purpose of this step is to validate that the uploaded document has been successfully analyzed before proceeding with application generation. Once the document analysis is completed successfully and the extracted summary has been reviewed, click Open Dashboard to proceed to the detailed review screen. The Open Dashboard button opens the Review Extracted Information dashboard, where users can: Review all extracted business components in detail. Verify entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, schedulers, menu access, and homepage configuration. Modify, add, or remove extracted items as required. Validate the extracted information before proceeding to the Execution Plan stage. Review Extracted Information​ This section provides categorized access to all the information extracted from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Each category displays the number of items identified during the analysis, allowing users to review every component before proceeding with application generation. The available categories include: Entities – Displays the entities extracted from the document. Screens – Lists the application screens identified during analysis. Schedulers – Displays scheduled jobs or background processes. Functional Requirements – Shows the extracted business requirements. Notifications – Lists notification and alert configurations. User Roles – Displays user roles identified for role-based access control. Menu Access – Shows the application's navigation menu structure. Homepage – Displays the extracted homepage configuration. Out of Scope – Lists requirements identified as outside the application's scope. AI Visualize – Provides AI-generated visual representations of the extracted business information. Ask BBP – An AI-powered assistant that answers questions related to the uploaded BBP. Selecting a category displays its corresponding details in the main content area for review. Note: At present, manual addition, modification, or deletion of extracted components is not supported. The entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, and other components displayed on this screen are generated by Developer AI based on the uploaded BRD or BBP and are used as the foundation for application generation. Users can review the extracted information before proceeding to the next step.

documents.t: Developer AI provides an option to export the extracted entity information for offline review or integration. Export to JSON​ The Export to JSON button downloads the extracted entity metadata in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format. The exported file contains structured information such as: Entity details Attributes Relationships Entity types Associated metadata The JSON format can be used for documentation, integration with external systems, or further processing. Export to TXT​ The Export to TXT option is currently not supported. Although the option is visible in the interface, exporting the extracted information in TXT format is not available in the current release and will be supported in a future version.

documents.t: The Re-Analyze button allows users to run the document analysis again if changes have been made to the uploaded BRD or BBP, or if the extracted results need to be refreshed. When clicked, Developer AI: Reprocesses the uploaded document. Extracts the latest business requirements and application components. Updates the extracted entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, menu access, and other information.

documents.t: The Mark All Review Completed button confirms that the extracted information has been reviewed and approved. Selecting this option indicates that: The extracted entities have been verified. Screens and functional requirements have been reviewed. User roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other extracted components have been validated. The application is ready to proceed to the next stage. Note: Marking the review as complete is mandatory before proceeding. If this step is not completed, an alert message will appear when you attempt to continue, prompting you to mark all reviews as completed before moving to the next stage.

documents.t: The Execution Plan button navigates to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. After the review is completed, clicking Execution Plan opens the Execution Plan screen, where Developer AI displays the sequence of activities required to generate the application. The Execution Plan provides an overview of: Components to be generated. Order of execution. This serves as the final review before Developer AI begins generating the application.

documents.t: The Refine BBP with AI feature is designed to allow users to improve or modify the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) using natural language instructions before proceeding with application generation. This option can be accessed by clicking the ✨ (AI Refine) button available on the Review Extracted Information screen.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: Click the ✨ (AI Refine) button. The Refine BBP with AI dialog is displayed. What should AI change? text box, enter the required modifications or enhancements in natural language. Examples: Tighten the module scope. Add missing approval rules. Correct notification triggers. Add a new business entity. Update the workflow for order approval. Click Apply AI Changes. Developer AI is designed to analyze the provided instructions and update the extracted BBP accordingly. The refined information would then be reflected in the extracted components for further review before proceeding with application generation. Note: The Refine BBP with AI feature is currently not supported in the current release. Although the option is available in the interface, AI-based refinement of the extracted BBP is not yet functional and will be supported in a future release.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: After clicking Execution Plan, the Review BBP Changes Before Build dialog is displayed. This screen provides a final summary of the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) before the application build process begins. The summary displays the number of: Existing in BBP – Components that were identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Added – New components that have been added during the review process. Updated – Components that have been modified before execution. The dialog also lists all the extracted application components, such as: Entities Screens Functional Requirements Notifications User Roles Other extracted artifacts This allows users to perform a final verification of the application metadata before proceeding with the build. Available Options Compare AI Changes – Displays a comparison between the original extracted information and any AI-generated changes (if applicable). Back to Review – Returns to the Review Extracted Information screen to make further changes or validations. Proceed to Execution Plan – Confirms the review and navigates to the Execution Plan screen, where the application generation workflow is initiated.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: After clicking Proceed to Execution Plan, the Execution Selection screen is displayed. This screen allows users to review all extracted components and select the items that should be included in the application generation process. A summary at the top of the screen displays the total number of extracted components, including: Entities UI Screens Schedulers Workflows Notifications User Roles Menu Access Homepage Each category shows the number of items identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: The lower section displays the extracted components grouped by category. Each item is accompanied by a checkbox, allowing users to choose whether it should be included in the application build. Users can: Review the extracted entities and screens. Select or deselect individual components. Use the Select All option to include all available components for generation. Only the selected components will be considered during the application generation process.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: After reviewing and selecting the required components, click Execute to start the application generation process. Developer AI begins generating the selected application components within the chosen Procify application. This includes creating the selected entities, screens, workflows, notifications, user roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other supported artifacts. Note: Ensure that all required components are selected before clicking Execute, as only the selected items will be included in the application generation process.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: After clicking Execute, the Execution Progress screen is displayed. This screen tracks the progress of the application generation process and shows the status of each component being created. To begin generating the application, click Build Application.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: The Build Application button initiates the application generation process based on the components selected in the Execution Plan. During the build process, Developer AI automatically creates and configures the selected application components, including: Business entities UI screens Value Helps Sample data Application roles Notifications Business rules Menus Homepage configuration Permissions Other supported application artifacts
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: As the build progresses, the Execution Progress section displays the status of each component. Each component is marked with one of the following statuses: In Progress – The component is currently being generated. Completed – The component has been successfully created. The progress cards provide a quick overview of the build status for each application component.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: The Execution Log records every step performed during the application generation process. The log includes information such as: Analysis completion Entity creation Screen generation Business rule creation Sample data insertion Role creation Menu generation Homepage configuration Permission assignment Any warnings or errors encountered during the build The execution log helps users monitor the build process and troubleshoot issues if required.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Developer AI - 4. ProcessFlow of Developer AI

documents.t: When all selected components have been generated successfully, the status changes to Build Completed. A confirmation message indicates that the application has been successfully created within the selected Procify application. Users can then click Continue to proceed to the next step in the Developer AI workflow. Note :- Build Queue Notification When a BBP build is triggered for an application while another BBP build is already in progress for a different application, the new build request is not started immediately. Instead, it is automatically placed in a system-wide queue and will begin execution once the currently running build is completed. Build Already in Progress If a BBP build is triggered for an application that already has an active build in progress, Developer AI does not start a new build for the same application. Instead, it notifies the user that a build is already running and provides an option to view the current build progress. Click Yes, Show Progress to open the ongoing build progress screen, or click Cancel to close the notification

documents.t: Entities After the application is generated, all the business entities created by Developer AI are automatically available in the Data Studio. These entities form the core data model of the generated application and can be reviewed and further configured as needed. The left navigation panel displays the list of all generated entities. Selecting an entity opens its complete configuration, where you can review its properties, relationships, business rules, workflows, access control, and other metadata. Note: If the generated entities are not immediately visible in the Data Studio, refresh the application or browser. The entities will be displayed once the latest metadata is loaded. Screens Developer AI automatically generates the required application pages based on the uploaded BRD/BBP. These pages provide the user interface for interacting with the generated business entities and application features. The generated pages are available in the Page Builder and can be reviewed, customized, or enhanced using the standard Procify page designer. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following pages: p_homepage_001 – The application's landing page that provides users with the initial view after logging in. p_dashboard_001 – Displays the application's dashboard, providing a consolidated view of key information, widgets, and business insights. p_delivery_mgmt – The Delivery Management page used to create, view, update, and manage delivery-related transactions. Role & Users The roles and users generated by Developer AI can be viewed from the Roles & Users section under the Details tab of the generated application in App Management. This section allows you to review the user roles and user assignments created for the application. Homepage Log in using one of the users created in the Roles & Users section. After successful login, the application opens the Homepage generated by Developer AI. The homepage displayed corresponds to the configuration defined in the Homepage component during the application generation process. It serves as the application's landing page and provides users with quick access to the generated modules, dashboards, and navigation menus based on their assigned role and permissions. Dashboard Developer AI automatically generates the application dashboard based on the requirements defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated dashboard provides users with a consolidated view of key business information, metrics, and navigation components relevant to the application. It is designed to offer quick access to important data and frequently used features immediately after login. The dashboard created by Developer AI can be accessed from the Dashboard menu within the generated application and can be further customized using the standard Procify dashboard designer to meet specific business requirements. Note: The layout, widgets, and overall design of the generated dashboard are determined by Developer AI based on its analysis of the uploaded BBP or BRD. Dashboard generation is AI-driven, and users cannot control or define the dashboard layout by providing screenshots or sample designs. To influence the generated dashboard, include clear and detailed dashboard requirements within the BBP or BRD. Menu Developer AI automatically generates the application's navigation menu based on the modules, screens, and user workflows defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP. The generated menu provides users with organized navigation to access the application's features. Menu items are created based on the business requirements and are assigned appropriate access according to the generated user roles and permissions. In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following menu items: Home – The default landing page that provides users with quick access to the application. My Deliveries – A module for managing and viewing delivery-related transactions. Dashboard – Provides access to the application's dashboard, displaying key business insights and summary information.

The Procify Landing Page Settings provides a robust, secure, and performant solution for creating dynamic homepage experiences. By following this documentation and implementing the recommended best practices, developers can create powerful, user-friendly homepage systems that scale with organizational needs while maintaining security and performance standards. For additional support or advanced configuration requirements, consult the Procify development team or refer to the latest API documentation. Note: KloGuid and KloLink controls will be disabled when added inside the embedded subscreens. Since the homepage uses embedded sections to display the screens, they will appear to be disabled as well. If required please use sap.m.Link control.

Select the flavor to create/see the homepages in that flavor. Once you select the flavor, the edit button will be enabled. If there are homepages in that flavor that will appear in the list. Once you have selected the flavor, it will persist even if you refresh and homepages in that flavor will be persisted 5. Click the Edit button to go into Edit Mode Once you Click the Edit button, the page will go to Edit Mode. You should now be able to see Add, Delete, Save and Cancel Buttons. 6 Click On Home Icon below the Hamburger Menu in the sidebar to navigate to Home Page If you have not added any Homepage entries in the Landing Page Settings, then Procify Logo with Procify text is shown below it 7 Click on + Add button A new homepage entry will be created Fill in the screen id in the page column by clicking the Value Help Icon and selecting the screen you like. Fill in the sequence and Tab Text. Click on Save. Once Save is successful the page will reload and You can click the Homepage button again to see the added Home Page. If one Homepage entry is added, then that homepage is shown in the screen. 8 Add another Homepage in another flavor Go to Landing Page Settings and Select a different flavor, Click on Edit to Go Into Edit mode. Click on +Add button. Fill the screen id and changed the Tab Text if you want. Go to the homepage. If there are more than one entries in homepage, then You will see a tab with icon and title (icon filled from the tab_icon and title will be filled from the tab_text fields of the Landing Page Settings) In Mobile, back button is removed and the title in the screen titlebar will be dynamically updated based on the currently selected tab and filled from the title property of the Landing Page Settings, if not provided then picked from the Tab Text otherwise screenid. Precedence: Tab Text=> Screen Title => Screen Id Precedence: Title => Tab Text => Screen Id If no homepages are added then the title “Home” is shown in the screen title bar. 9 Now in the roles field, select the role other than the role currently assigned to the user Here the app is assigned as TESTER to the user but we are selecting as manager Since the role doesn’t match, the screen is not shown to the user i.e., it is hidden from the user. 10 Add permissions to your entity Create a permission group in Role Permissions if it doesn’t exist Enable Excel Download permission for testing purpose. Then Go to Landing Page Settings and In Edit Mode, Select the required permission from the Permissions dropdown. Then if the permissions is valid, then the Homepage is Visible otherwise it won’t be visbile NOTE: Make sure that all the permissions are assigned for all the users by default, even after assigning the permissions to the homepage and permission not given and homepage is still showing up then remove the permission group “flv_master_grp” from the Role Permissions screen for your user role. 11 You can trim the subscreen by passing Page Parameters. Eg: {"trimSubscreen": "s_notif_t_detail"}. Here s_notif_t_detail is the detail section’s subscreenid 12 We can change the Icon which is shown in the Tab of the HomeScreen.

The Menu Editor table includes a search field above the menu tree to help locate a specific Menu ID or Menu Text quickly. How search works: The search matches against both Menu ID and Menu Text, and applies partial/fuzzy matching — you don't need to type the exact full value. If your search term matches a parent menu item only, the filtered tree shows just that parent row (its children are not pulled into the result unless they also match). If your search term matches a child menu item, the filtered tree shows that child along with its parent, so you always retain context of where the item sits in the hierarchy. Note on the child-count indicator: The number shown next to a parent menu item always reflects the total number of children that parent actually has in the full menu tree — not just the ones currently visible in your search results. This count does not change based on your search filter. For example, searching for a parent's name may show a count of 3 even though none of those 3 children match your search text and are therefore not shown below it. Tip: To view all children of a parent, clear the search field (or expand the node directly) rather than relying on the search result or the count next to it.
