Middleware (Message Monitoring) is an application that is used for fetching all the information about the entries that are present in the device Info or tenant Info. We can also reprocess the failed messages present inside the error_q of the tenant. Device Info: When we are sending any data/action from server to device we store the message in the device info to know its information and state. In device info, every message is an outgoing message. So, the successfully sent messages are shown here. So, It goes from In queue to success. Tenant Info: When we are sending/fetching any data/action from server to SAP LOCAL or sending data from device to server. We store the message in tenant info to know its information and state. All the messages from Device to Server and SAP Local to server are visible in Inbound MessagesServer Queue Monitor screen. All the messages from Server to SAP Local will be visible to the Outbound queue screen and all the messages from server to device or SAP Local to device will be visible in Device OutboundDevice Queue Monitor screen. Purpose of Message Monitoring​ Message Monitoring is used to show information about messages (UPGRADE, DEBOARD) and the state of the message whether it's in the in-queue, Success, or failed. Every message has a state out of the three states mentioned below : In-Queue: The message is ready for processing. Success: The message has been processed successfully. Failed: Message processing has failed. We can also reprocess the Failed message. The reprocess function is only available for tenant_q. When we are sending/fetching any data/Action from server to device or server to SAP local, we store it in terms of messages to know its information and its state. An Upsert operation refers to the combination of update and insert actions, where data is either updated if it exists or inserted if it doesn't. When syncing messages, an Upsert scenario behavior typically involves checking if a message already exists in the destination system or database. If it exists, the system will update it; if it doesn't, the system will insert it as a new record. 1.5.1.Upsert Behavior in Middleware for Syncing Messages:​ Data Creation and Update: If the data is new (does not exist in the system), a new entry will be created. If the data already exists, the existing record will be updated instead of creating a new one. Upsert for Root Business Objects (BOs) and Primary Relations: Upsert is only applicable for Root Business Objects (BOs) and their primary relations. For non-primary relations, the Upsert operation will work only if the relation is established using primary keys. Parent-Child Relationship: If a parent is new, but the child data related to the parent already exists, this is considered an unexpected scenario. The user must handle this manually, as it is not automatically managed by the middleware. 1.5.2.Delete Scenario Behavior:​ Parent Entity Deletion: If the parent entity is deleted, the child entities will only be deleted if the user explicitly sends the isdeleted flag as true in the request body for both the parent and child entities. This applies to both primary and aggregate relationships. Child Entity Deletion: If the child entity is deleted, only the child will be deleted. The parent entity will remain intact.

Messages that are failed to process can be found in the error q. The error can be found in the error message. Possible reasons a message can fail are. Application logic - When an application logically rejects a request for processing the message. I.e. Adding items to a closed order. Adding shipments to a closed Delivery etc. Suggested solution : Find the root cause why these messages are generated. Eg. screen still allows adding items even if the status of order is closed. And fix the issue / add validation in the client side also. Application bugs - Some cases where application code has a bug, due to which an exception can be raised the message will fail. Eg. Improper null handling, wrong API parameters, typo etc. Transaction User not configured - File processing, transaction user has to be configured with required application & permissions. As all the messages are processed based on the access of the user, messages generated by files need a user to validate against. Refer to the Landscape Editor for how to configure the transaction user. Configured user doesn’t have application assigned : When messages from SAP / File processing are failing with “Access denied: user lacks permission to the required application.” error, it means, the user (SAP communication user / File processing user) does not have that flavor assigned to them. Database Deadlock / Lock Timeout Errors: - When the middleware encounters a transient database deadlock or lock wait timeout (e.g., "Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction"), messages are automatically retried up to 3 times with a 1-second delay (default values) between attempts. - If all retries are exhausted, the message will move to the error queue. - It will have an error message like - "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Lock wait timeout exceeded" or "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Deadlock found". - The retry settings are configurable via config.json: "MiddlewareRetrySettings": { "DeadlockRetryCount": 3, "RetryDelaySeconds": 1 }

When an application team logs in from multiple or random devices without properly deboarding the previous devices, those devices can continue to be considered active endpoints. As a result, messages may continue to be generated for these endpoints even though the application team is no longer actively using them. Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Whenever any new user registers in the application, a new endpoint ID is created against that account... when they log in again the status becomes Active." Each login is a distinct endpoint; none are deregistered automatically on crash or app closure.
documents.s: 2.1. Multiple Logins Can Create Active Endpoints

documents.t: Because these endpoints remain active, messages generated for them may not be synchronized with the device immediately. Over time, a large number of messages can accumulate in the queue. This can give the impression that a large number of messages are stuck. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — In-Queue is defined as "all the data that are currently present in the device_q and which are not processed yet." A high In-Queue count reflects endpoints awaiting sync, not failed or lost messages.
documents.s: 2.2 Messages Can Accumulate in the Queue

documents.t: When the corresponding device comes online , the queued messages are synchronized with the device. Once the server successfully sends the messages and receives the required acknowledgment from the client, the messages move to Success. If the device is offline, the messages remain in the queue until the device becomes available. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — device_q entries move to device_log_q (Success) or device_error_q (Failed) only after processing; until then they remain In-Queue, consistent with holding messages for an offline device until it reconnects.
documents.s: 2.3. Messages Are Synchronized When the Device Becomes online

documents.t: A message can reach the device successfully, but the actual processing on the device may still fail. From the server's perspective, the message can be marked as Success when the client acknowledges that the message was received while the device was online. Therefore, Success on the server does not necessarily mean that the message was successfully processed by the application on the device. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — "In device info, every message is sent or is in the process of being successfully sent. So, every message is outgoing and never fails. Hence, It goes from in-queue to success." This confirms Success tracks the send/acknowledgment, not on-device application processing.

The application team may not be aware that previously used devices are still registered as active endpoints. This can result in messages continuing to be generated and queued for those endpoints. Note: This is a training/visibility gap rather than a platform defect. Recommend making Sections 1–4 of this topic available to application teams so "stuck message" reports can be self-diagnosed before being escalated as incidents.

A scheduler runs every Sunday to clean up old endpoints. Note: The scheduler currently deboards endpoints that have been inactive for more than 7 days. Once an endpoint is deboarded, its corresponding entry is removed from the endpoint table. Property Value Class name deboardInactiveUsers CRON expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN * (every Sunday at midnight) Current inactivity threshold (this environment) 7 days Platform default threshold 15 days — this environment has been configured below the default Channel type BOTH, unless restricted to DEVICE or BROWSER Table cleaned up Endpoint's entries removed from madm_ep_apps Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Deboard Inactive Users": CRON Job Expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN *, class deboardInactiveUsers, parameters No_of_inactive_days {default: 15} and Channel_type {default: BOTH}; "this scheduler will deboard all the users who are inactive since given days and it will delete the entry of all deboarded endpoints from madm_ep_apps."

If the default 7-day cleanup period does not meet the application's requirements, the scheduler can be customized to use a different endpoint deboarding period. To change it: Go to the job-instances page in Cockpit and locate the deboardInactiveUsers job. Open the job instance's parameters. Update No_of_inactive_days to the desired threshold. Update Channel_type if the cleanup should be restricted to a specific channel. Save. The new threshold takes effect on the job's next scheduled run (the following Sunday, per the fixed CRON expression). Note: The CRON schedule itself (currently fixed to Sunday) is a separate setting from the inactivity threshold — changing how often the job runs, as opposed to how many inactive days it waits, would need to be confirmed as in-scope for this customization request.

Overview The Middleware Message Forwarding feature allows you to automatically sync data changes between different flavors of your application. When data is changed in one flavor (source), it can automatically trigger message generation for users of another flavor (target), ensuring all users stay synchronized regardless of which flavor they're using.

Multi-Flavor Setup​ ✅ You must have multiple flavors (source and target flavors) ✅ Both source and target flavors must be deployed and accessible ✅ Flavors should share common entities that require message sync Entity Design​ ✅ Target Entity: Must exist with identical entity name and table name ✅ Target Entity: Must have ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event configured with proper implementation

Administrative Access​ ✅ Access to Operations Monitor application for configuration ✅ Permissions to create/modify Middleware Message Routing entries ✅ Message monitoring access for troubleshooting and monitoring Development Environment​ ✅ Private node setup with DEV landscape (for testing) ✅ Access to both source and target flavor codebases ✅ Debugging capabilities in development environment

Message Processing Infrastructure​ ✅ Message processing must be functional Monitoring Tools​ ✅ Message Monitoring screen access for tracking forwarded messages ✅ Queue Monitor for viewing message queues and error queues ✅ Log access for troubleshooting and debugging

Development Team​ ✅ Understanding of entity event implementation (ENDPOINT_RESOLVER) ✅ Familiarity with addEndpoint() method usage ✅ Knowledge of message queue and processing ✅ Experience with multi-flavor application development Configuration Team​ ✅ Understanding of flavor versioning and deployment ✅ Knowledge of landscape management (DEV/TEST/PROD) ✅ Familiarity with Operations Monitor configuration tools

To enable message forwarding, you need to configure mappings in the Mw Message Routing Screen in Operations Monitor: Configuration Screen - Mw Message Routing Access this screen through Operations Monitor > Middleware Message Routing Required Fields​ Source Flavor: The flavor where changes originate Target Flavor: The flavor that where the changes should be also be forwarded for message generation. Is Active: Set to true to enable forwarding Target Version: Only for DEV Specify a particular version of the target flavor. Use this for debugging purposes. In QA & Production, the latest version is used. Configuration Steps​ Open Operations Monitor application Navigate to "Middleware Message Routing" Click "Add New" to create a mapping Fill in Source Flavor and Target Flavor names Set "Is Active" to true Save the configuration

documents.t: Multi-Flavor Applications​ If your application has multiple flavors (e.g., online and offline versions) that share common entities, this feature ensures data consistency across all flavors. Example Scenarios:​ Portal + Mobile App: Changes made in the web portal should sync to mobile app users Hierarchical Applications: Parent flavor changes should sync to child flavor users How Does It Work ?​ Data Change Trigger: When you create, update, or delete data in a source flavor Automatic Detection: The system detects if forwarding is configured for that flavor in Middleware Message Routing ( Operations Monitor ) Trigger Endpoint Resolver: The ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event will be triggered in target flavor if the same entity exists. Message Generation: Messages are generated for target flavor users based on the target flavor ENDPOINT_RESOLVER logic. Synchronized Delivery: All related messages share the same reference ID for tracking

What is kloTouch? kloBase platform is a modern low-code platform to build enterprise-class cloud-enabled portals and mobile business applications. Its unique layered development empowers to build powerful reusable models for the continuously evolving business needs. kloTouch is a low-code visual designer tool that helps application development efficiently and effectively. What is the objective of kloTouch? kloTouch is a visual designing Page Builder that is effective in building applications that work on portals and mobile applications. kloTouch has the following objectives: Ease of Operating: It involves least to no complex coding, thus, making it an easy-to-use tool, not only for the modellers but also for common people with limited technical knowledge. Efficient: This Page Builder is programmed in a manner that requires a limited to negligible coding process. This prevents the modellers and developers from losing time by writing lengthy codes, thus saving time. Rich In-Built Features: Multiple add-ons and real-time notifications to name a few, help make it a featureful application.

For Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid section types, the Builder automatically applies horizontal alignment (hAlign) and text align property based on the control type and its associated binding. So the column header and the control will be aligned as per the standards based on the domain and control type Numeric Field Alignment​ If a control is bound to a property whose domain type is Integer or Decimal, the Builder automatically adds the hAlign config property and textAlign control property with the value Right. This automatic alignment is applied only when: The control is an input-based control. The control is bound to a property of domain type Integer or Decimal. Alignment Updates on Control Changes​ During updates, if: A control's value property or dsrc is modified, or A new binding is added to the control, the Builder automatically detects the bound property and updates the alignment accordingly.

documents.t: The App selection drop-down contains a list of apps that have been assigned to the user. By using the drop-down users can select the app on which they are going to work.

The page selection drop-down is used to select the page. The page dropdown will list all the pages available for the app that have been selected. Note:This drop-down will be visible only when the app is selected.
The Create Page has three parts: Create Blank Page Create a Page From Wizard Update Page From Wizard Make A Copy of Page The Create page option is to create a new page for the selected app.
The undo option is to revert the changes that were made. The use of the redo option is to redo the changes that are undone.
The painter can be used to copy a property or style or vienable of one control to another/multiple controls.

Step 1: Select any control/section from the page tree section Step 2: select the option from the painter Property - all the property details of the selected item will be copied Style - all the styles added to the selected item will be copied Vienable - all the vienable applied to the selected property will be copied Step 3: Now select the control/section in the page tree to which the copied items should be pasted. Note: With the painter option, we can apply the copied items to multiple elements, so once the items are pasted, click on `Esc`.

The Save option is used to save the changes that are done. Note:Save button will be visible only in edit mode. The Edit option is used to make the kloEditor modifiable. 1.8 Read-Only and Cancel {#1.8-read-only-and-cancel} The Read-Only and Cancel option is only visible in editable mode. Clicking read-only mode locks the editor in making further changes. On click of the cancel icon, any changes made in the editor that are not yet saved will be reverted.
This button will validate the page. Note:It will be visible only in edit mode.

Section toggle buttons are used to make the sections hide / visible. Each toggle button is described below: This is the tree button. This is used to show the hierarchy of the page sectionally. With a click of this button, it will hide the tree section. However, if you click back it will show the tree section again. This is the preview button. This shows a live view of the changes that have been made to the page. With a click of this button, the preview will disappear. However, on clicking it again the preview section will reappear. This is the Detail button. The detail section shows the details for the selected item in the tree (page hierarchy). On clicking this button the detail section will disappear. On clicking it again the section will reappear. Page data model which is equivalent to the UI5 Model in the view. On clicking this button the section will disappear. On clicking it again the page data model section will reappear. This is the Reset Perspective button. As the name suggests, this is used to resize the section into its original position.

To delete the page or screen, a shortcut key will only work, using ALT + BCKSPC . It will display a confirmation dialog box, confirming to delete the entire page or to cancel the delete as shown below.
Klotouch Editor is divided into four major sections, which are listed below. Tree Preview Detail Page Data Model

The tree section in the kloTouch editor contains the hierarchy of the page. The tree will contain no data unless a page is created/selected from the toolbar. Once a page is created/selected it shall automatically reflect in the tree section.
Expand All option is to expand all the collapsed sections (sections, pageLayout, controls, pageArea, actions).
Collapse All option is to collapse all the expanded sections (sections, pageLayout, wcontrols, pageArea, actions).

This filter button will open a popup as : It will contain fuzzy search, section drop-down and clear filter option. The use of fuzzy search is to filter the items based on the Ids. Section dropdown is used to select and preview a particular section / pageArea of the page. This will filter the tree only for the selected section and its children. Clear filters are used to clear the filters applied.
Using the cut copy-paste options, we are able to copy paste the controls/section /pageAreas. **Note:** These buttons are inactive in read-only mode.

The create section button is used to create a section and to add required properties from a particular type of transnode. Clicking on this button, it will open a popup : In the above popup, we need to mention section id, section title, section type and page data model with which the section is supposed to be binded. After selecting the page data model, properties list will come in the Page Data Model Node section from where we can select the required properties. Note: We can edit the section after creation from the Editor.
The Preview section is to preview the page before the final execution.

This is also known as the Preview type. The use of preview types is to see the look and feel of the same page on different types of devices. The devices that it can be viewed on are given below. Any new version of the device comes, likewise, it will be updated. Preview samples

Usage of the auto-refresh button is to refresh the preview in design time i.e. if the auto-refresh is enabled whenever the user changes anything in the page’s metadata it will be previewed (auto-refreshed) automatically.
The usage of the preview or refresh button is to refresh the preview page to make the changes visible.
The full preview option is used to view the page in full view.
The close option is to hide the preview section, to enable the preview section make use of the section toggle buttons Buttons Identity To Expand to Full Screen. To Close the Preview Section.

DnD on Preview is a drag-and-drop feature. It is an option to Drag and Drop properties and elements in multiple ways. DnD from Unused to MainTree: Step 1: From the page data model, select the transnode, go to its unused property tab and drag the Property. Step 2: Drop that Property to any section you want. After preview, the newly added property will be shown on the screen. DnD from MainTree to MainTree: Users can Drag and Drop any main tree element across the tree. Step 1: Drag an element from any section and Drop it into the different sections in the same tree. When an element is dragged and dropped between sections, a prompt appears asking whether to Move or Copy the element. Selecting Move removes the element from the source section and places it in the target section, while selecting Copy duplicates the element in the target section without affecting the source. Note: The Move and Copy options are shown only when the drag-and-drop action occurs between two different sections.
Details of the item selected in the tree section will be shown in this detail section: This depicts the name or ID of the item selected in the tree.

The property tab in the detail section displays the properties that are added and options to add new properties that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, pageLayout, sections, controls). Refer to this to understand binding concepts. Value:​ The value field will hold the value provided for the property. Path:​ In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. This can be used if there is only one property to bind. Parts:​ In this path field, users can bind multiple properties or values. This can be used if multiple values or properties need to be provided for binding. (Note: If we are using formatter function, then it is mandatory to provide either parts or path value) Formatter Functions​ Controller function name (formatter function) can be given for the field. Type:​ In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value. Formatter Options:​ Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI. Validation Constraint:​ Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values. Add new Property:​ To add a new property, click on the add icon in the property section toolbar. On click of the add icon the properties associated with the control will be listed. Click on the property that needs to be added, it will be added to the control. Provide the property value for the newly added property. ​ Property Group:​ The Property group consists of the following: Property Group Details Appearance The appearance property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the appearance of the control. Example: visible, textAlign, wrapping, textDirection. Data The data property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the binding values of the control. Example: value, src, text, href. Dimension Dimension property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the dimensions of the control. Example: width, size, height. Behaviour The behaviour property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the behaviour of a control. Example: editable, enabled. Misc Properties other than the above-mentioned groups will come under Misc. Select All/ None:​ This option is used to select/unselect all the properties. Cut:​ This option is to cut and paste the property of one control to another control. Copy and Paste:​ The Copy and Paste options are used to copy/paste one or more properties from one control to another. Delete Property:​ To delete a property, select the property that needs to be deleted and click on the delete icon in the properties section toolbar. **![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image13.png)**

The Aggregations tab in the detail section displays the aggregations that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls) Path:​ Binding Path addresses the different properties and lists in a model and defines how a node in the hierarchical data tree can be found. Examples: $M>/list, $M>/items Add new Aggregation:​ To add a new aggregation click on the add icon in the aggregation section toolbar. On click of the add icon the aggregations associated with the control will be listed. Click on the aggregation that needs to be added, it will be added to the control. Select All/ None​ This option is being used to select/unselect all the aggregations. Cut​ This option is to cut and paste the aggregations of one control into another control. Copy and Paste​ The Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more aggregations from one control to another. Delete Aggregation:​ For delete, select the aggregation that you want to delete. And click on the delete icon in the aggregation toolbar.

The Events tab in the detail section displays the events that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls). Functions​ The controller function name should be given in the field, which will be called in case of the event. Example of Controller function: ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image14.png) Parameters​ The values passed in the field can be accessible in the function as a parameter. Add new Event:​ To add a new event click on the add icon in the event section toolbar. On click of the add icon the events associated with the control will be listed. Click on the event that needs to be added, it will be added to the control/sections / pageArea. Note: If we are adding a new event then, it is necessary to add or select the function name. If we are adding a function from the vh as OpenDialog, it will show a popup with all the pageAreas to select,from which we want to navigate. Select All/ None:​ This option is being used to select/unselect all the events. Cut:​ This option is to cut and paste the event of one control to another control. Copy and Paste:​ Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more events from one control to another. Delete Event:​ To delete an event select the event and click on the delete button from the toolbar. Events list on page In the page-level events, we have an option to see the list of events added to this page. Step 1: Select the page in the Page Builder page tree section Step 2: Select the events tab in the page detail section Step 3: enable the toggle button Once it is enabled, all the events added to this page will be listed below

NavTo is a kloController API that is used for navigation across the application. In the Events tab of the Page Builder, if we select NavTo as an event method, the below parameters will reflect for NavTo. Parameters for Navigation​ The following are the parameters for the navigation: Target Page: It is an F4 of the screens where sections of the current screen, related screen (screens created with related entities) and all the screens of the respected app are present. Section: It is an F4 of all the pagelayouts, pageAreas and sections of the target page. Tags: It shows all the TagIDs maintained in the target screen. Mode: It is a dropdown for different screen modes. App Data: It is a field where the application can send any data while navigating to the target screen. Page Data Model: It is a F4 of all the Data models of the target page. Active Index: It accepts the index to which setActive will be called in the list. Page Data Model Map: It is an array of JSON which expect SourceTransNode & TargetTransnode(i.e SourcetransNode data will be copied to TargetTransnode) Query Parameters: It is for navigation by query(navByQuery). Share Mode: This is for setting whether the mode will be shared after navigating between the source and target pages. Share Model: This is for setting whether the transaction will be shared after navigating between the source and target page.

The Style Class tab in the detail section displays the quick styles that are available for the control/pageArea/sections. There are style classes that have already been added and there are options to add a new style class for the selected item (pageArea, sections, controls). QuickAdd:​ Quick Add for Sections:​ Below is the list of quick adds available for specific section types: Section types Quick Adds Card, card List Card styles Grid Grid styles ​ Card Styles:​ Grid Styles:​ Quick Add for Controls:​ Below is the list of quick adds available for specific controls: Controls Quick Add Icon Font size, Text color Text, Label, Title, Link Font size, Text color, Bold, Italic, Underline Button, Switch, info label Font Size, Background color, Text Color, color combination, Bold, Italic, underline, border style Input, TextArea, DatePicker, TimePicker, DateTimePicker, MultiCombobox, MultiInput, SearchField, comboBox Font size, Text color, Bold, Italic, Underline, border style Font Size:​ Text Colour:​ Bold:​ Italic:​ Underline:​ Background color:​ Color Combination:​ Specific Style:​ Category:​ In this category field, we can choose the style category that needs to be applied to the selected item. Style Class:​ Class names should be provided for this field, which will be applied to the selected items. Style class works after selecting the category. In the below image, we have taken the border as our category. Hence, border options are seen in the StyleClass. Note: The style class should not be empty. Format Rule: Always: If the format rule is marked as always, it will always apply the style. Text Contains: If the format rule is marked as the text contains, it will apply the style if the value contains the one mentioned in the format value. Formula: If the format rule is marked as formula, it will apply the expression maintained in the format value field and based on the result set of the expression (result is expected to be true or false) the style class will be applied to that control Example Format value for formula : {= ${$M>/temp/save}?true:false} Format Value:​ If the format rule is marked with text contain, then text will be taken from this format value field and it will be compared with the control’s value. If the format rule is marked with a formula, then the expression will be taken from this format value field and based on the result set(the result should be expected to be true or false) of the expression, the style class will be set. **Example Format value for formula** : {= \${\$M\>/temp/save}?true:false} Full Row:​ If the full row is marked as true, then the style class will be applied to the entire row, where the control is placed. Note: For tree screen type, full-row in style class will be applicable only when the section’s screen type is full row, it will not work for control for control type tree tables. Add new Style Class:​ To add a new style class click on the add icon in the style class section toolbar. On clicking the add icon, a new entry will be created for the style class. Select the category and add the style class accordingly. Cut, copy, and paste:​ For cut, copy, and paste you need to select the styleclass and then use the cut, copy, and paste accordingly. Delete​ Select the StyleClass item you want to delete and then click on the delete icon from the toolbar. Grid Cell Coloring:​ For adding css(background) to whole cell of grid section, user can do following: Add user defined class in control of grid section use :has Pseudo-class, and do required styling Example: as given below: td:has(.invAmountColorWholeCell) { background: \#0c8123; }

Vienable is the short form of visible and enable. The Vienable tab in the detail section displays the vienable dashboard and UI Auth for the page. Toolbar:​ Page Entity:​ Copy and paste:​ Upload and Download Excel:​ Role Info:​ Status Info:​ Vienable toggle button Info:​ ​ 2.3.5(i). Vienable DashBoard:​ ​ Control ID:​ The Control ID column displays the available controls on the page. Entity:​ The transNode of which the control is bound. If it is not marked as true, status and role-based vienable will not work. Permission:​ The permission of the entity in flavor on which control/element visibility will be decided for logged-in users. If permission is not filled by developer, then proceeds with with vienable calculation If permission is filled by developer, but filled permission not given for logged in user, then the current control/element will be hidden by skipping vienable calculation If permission is filled by developer, filled permission given for logged in user, then proceeds with with vienable calculation Show As Label:​ If the control is disabled, and the showAsLabel is marked as true then the disabled control will be rendered as a label. Page Size(S, M, L, XL):​ The page sizes S, M, L, and XL define small, medium, large, and extra-large size page resolutions. If the control is marked as non-visible for page size S, then the control will be hidden for that particular resolution. If the control is marked as disabled for page size S, then the control will be disabled for that particular resolution. Note: The resolution will be considered based on the parent section’s resolution for control. page Mode (Create, Edit, Display, Review):​ There are four modes for a page: Create, Edit, Display, and Review. Among the page modes display will be the default mode. We can change the page modes based on the requirements. ​ Role:​ Role-based vienable helps the control to be visible/enabled based on the current logged-in person’s role and object type of the bound entity. For this role-based configuration, KloTuner is used. For role-based vienable, config has to be maintained for the respective entity. If it is not maintained in the entity level, It will consider the role maintained in the app-level. While configuring the config table, provide the s_role_rollup value as below: Role s_role_up Owner 10 Supervisor 20 Reviewer 30 Overlooker 40 Status Group():​ ​ Status: open, approved, accepted, processed, rejected, completed. Based on the s_status_group, s_status, and object type for that particular entity, we will be able to make the control visible/enabled. For status-based configuration, Klotuner is used. Note: Similar to role-based vienable, status-based vienable status configs have to be maintained for the entity. ​ Result:​ In the result column, we can see the final result of how the controls will be rendered, for the selected page mode, selected role, and selected status group. The yellow background in the column header represents the selection of the column. 2.3.5(ii). UI Auth:​ Element Id:​ It is the control ID of the control. Object Type:​ For this object type, UI Auth will be applied. Role:​ For this role, the UI Auth will be applied. Status:​ For this status, UI Auth will be applied. Mode:​ For this mode, UI Auth will be applied. Mode Value:​ This will determine the control’s visibility / enableness. Add new UI Auth:​ To add a new UI Auth click on the add icon in the toolbar of the UI Auth section. On click of the add icon, a popup will be displayed. In the popup select the control for which UI Auth needs to be applied. Select the role, mode, object type, and status after selecting press OK. A new entry will be added in the UI Auth section. Vienable Runtime precedence:​ If all the vienable sections (screen size, screen mode, role, status) are maintained for control, below will be the flow of the section it will take into consideration.

The Modeller tab in the detail section displays the modeller only if the modeller is available for the selected section type. A modeller is generally used for modelling the sections. Note: The modeller will load only if the particular section is visible in the preview section. To access the modeller of a section select that particular section in the tree section to preview that particular section. Card & cardList Modeller:​ WYSWYG (What You See What You Get) Card WYSWYG allows the users to arrange/resize controls of the Card. The Card WYSWYG is available in the tab called “Modeller” of the kloTouch Editor if the section type is given as cardlist/card. These are the following steps to use WYSWYG: Step 1: Select the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”) or any child of the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”). Step 2: Open the “Modeller” tab. Users can arrange/resize controls as required. Step 3: For arranging the controls, the user can simply drag a control and drop it anywhere on the axis as per the requirement. While doing the arrangement or resizing, if any other control exists in the same axis, red lines will be shown. Step 4: For resizing the controls, Users can simply click on the controls and resize them as they want. Before resizing: After resizing: NOTE: Users can select multiple controls(by holding the control) and “Make the same size” (Vertically/Horizontally). Reveal Grid: With this button, one can enable and disable the gridlines. Tabular Card Modeller: On clicking this button, a tabular card modeller will open where the user can manually provide a column/row span for the alignment of the card/cardList. Alignment: Options for Alignment, space distribution, equal size: Modeller Size: To make the card modeller screen size the selected item’s size one uses the modeller size (Tab, Desktop, etc) tab.(This option has been disabled: To use this, change the screen resolution from preview type) Absolute/Relative: The absolute button will make the modeller as the previous version without additional features. On the other hand, the Relative button will set the modeller section as the newer version(5.7) with all the additional features. The card is generally a css gridlayout and the cardlist is generally a list of css grid layouts. Screen Size Spans available XL, L 36 column span M 24 column span S 12 column span For more information about CSS grid layout click here Note: if column span and row span are not maintained for a particular screen size then it will pick from the default span (if maintained). But if either of the one is maintained then it will pick both the values from that particular screen size. Note: As the Page Area of type Dialog doesn’t have any direct assignment with any of the page Layouts, the Modeler/preview will not be available.This Modeling can be achieved by adding that particular section to any other page Area (which is assigned to any page Layout). Once the modelling is completed, reassign to the Dialog Page Area. Grid Modeller:​ Grid modeller is used to model the grid type section. Using this grid modeller we will be able to change the column width, we can assign filters, and sort for a particular column. Pivot Modeller:​ There are two types of pivot modellers Design time Run time Note: The difference between the design time and run time modeller is that the design time modeller cannot be modified by end users it is predefined by the developers. The design time pivot can be set as the default view of the section by use of the ‘default report’ property of the section. Design Time Modeller :​ Design time pivot will be created by the developers which will be predefined, and cannot be modified by the end users. Step 1: Select a section which is of type card list or grid type and then add the report Step 2: Select the newly created record and click on the modeller to see the design time pivot modeller. Note: For how to use it you can refer to this document Pivot Modeller Run Time Modeller:​ The pivot modeller is used to configure the grid and card list subscreen. You can customise the pivots and charts based on your preferences, using this modeller. These are the following steps to enable the run time Pivot Modeller: Step 1: Select a section which is a card list or grid type and then add a toolbar to that subscreen. Step 2: Now in the toolbar detail, add two properties (reportSelectionField and pivotModellerButton) and mark these properties as true. Once the above properties are added during the design time, the modeller button and view selection will appear in the toolbar of the table during runtime. Note: For how to use it you can refer to this document Pivot Modeller CSS Grid:​ CSS grid is the screen container that can hold page areas or sections. Under CSS Grid, users can arrange subscreen controls in any way they want in any layout. Step 1: Make the Page Layout or Page Area screen type as ‘CSS Grid’. Step 2: Right-click on that page layout or page area and add the page layout data to it. After assigning the page section or PageArea, the page layout or page Area will look like this. Step 3: Now go to Modeller then click on ‘Tabular card Modeller’. Step 4: Add row/column-span to align subscreens as you want.

Language toolbar​ Components Description Language Dropdown (Select Language) This will list all the available languages in the dropdown. On selection of a language a new column will be displayed with the selected languages. Editable Language This will display all the selected languages from the language dropdown. Once the language is selected the language column will be editable. Search This will filter the grid rows of the text ID table. Add To add a new item or entity to the Item grid table. Translate To translate all the selected items that have been added to the row of the table. Show/Hide References It will hide/display the reference column. The reference column displays the destination where a particular textID has been placed. Add a new Entry​ Step 1 - Click on the Add Button To add a new entry/text click on the add button () on the Language toolbar. A Dialog box will appear. Step 2 - Fill the Dialog box In the Dialog box we need to give a TextID (Example: Header, Text, Caption, etc) and choose a category from the category list. Then click on OK. Category Description Text This refers to normal text labels for any text that has been added in the editor. Tooltip The tooltip helps in showcasing short descriptions about a particular entity or entry when the cursor is hovered over them. Title This represents the Normal title. TextID This represents the text ID. Ghosttext (PlaceHolder) This represents the texts in any kind of Input box. Text will be added to the screen. Editing the Languages:​ Select the languages that need to be made editable in the language dropdown and in the editable languages dropdown, to make the column editable. Translation:​ Step 1 - Select the Texts that are to be translated Select the items from the grid that need to be translated. Step 2 - Select the dropdown Editable Language Select the dropdown Editable Language (target Language) and choose the language to which you want the selected items to be changed. Note: The source language will be English as default. Also here English is referred to as en and Hindi is referred to as hi. Step 3 - Translate the Language Click on the translate button to translate to the required language. ​ Reference:​ Reference sections display where the text ID is being used. By default, the reference section will be hidden. To enable the reference section click on the reference button in the toolbar.

Tag Id​ Unique tag ID for the tag created Target Page​ On click of the Target page Value help, a selection popup will be displayed below This Page​ Will list all the PA, PL, and Sections of the current page, on selection, selected item will be populated Relation Page​ This will list all the relation pages which are associated with the leadEntity of the current page. All Page​ This will list all the pages available in the current app PL / PA / Section​ On click of the value help it will list all the page layouts, page area and sections of the selected page Mode​ Mode represents the page mode(Create, Edit, Delete, Review) Share Mode​ With the click of the share button, share mode is enabled, if the share mode is enabled the mode will be shared with the target pages. ​ Mode selection: If any mode is selected from the dropdown then the selected mode will be applied to the target page. Page Data Model​ Page Data Model Vh will list the all the transcodes available in the target page Query Parameters​ Query parameters which need to be passed. The query parameters will be applied to the advanced search of the target page transnode. (only if target page’s navByQuery is maintained) Share Model​ ​ App Data​ Application Data(AD) is received by the application as a parameter of the onAppDataProcess method Page Data Model Map​ Trasnode mapping-Transnode will be mapped from the source transnode to the target transnode. In the page data model map, the source and target transnode can be mapped from the value help popup.

Node Types in TransNode:​ Type Description Query Entity Set Entity Other Relations of selected TransNode:​ Properties of selected TransNode:​ TransNode Properties:​ Page Data Model(Expanded):​ The Hierarchy:​ ​ ​ Columns Description Hierarchy Displays the transNodes search, list and detail. Action Entity/Query Displays the entity name/query name of the transNode. Data Type Displays the data type of the used properties. Text ID Displays the textId of the used properties. Each property has its specific text ID. Width To set the width of the entity property when it is rendered. Link From Displays which transNode it is folded from. Set Active If Refer to Set_active_if onArrive Refer to onArrive Grid Allowed Will display the grid configuration of the used properties. More ​ Collapse all & Expand all:​ Collapse all option is used to collapse all the expanded sections (sections, sections, controls, containers, actions). Expand all options are used to expand all the collapsed sections(sections, controls, containers, actions). Add Model Path:​ By using the add model path button we will be able to create a new model path for the page. Model Path/TransNode:​ Properties Description Entity This field will display the entity name that is associated with the transNode. Property Description Displays the property description. folded_from This field will display from where the path is folded. node_type Node Type determines the type of the model path. on_arrive Refer to onArrive. q_auto_update If this is marked as true, then any change in the transactional data will be automatically updated in the model. q_object_group The Object group mentioned here will be filtered for the particular query type. q_object_type The object type mentioned here will be filtered for the particular query type. q_pin Coming Soon q_saved_qur_action Refer to q_saved_qur_action q_saved_qur_id This implicates the saved query ID which needs to be fired along with the search (if q_saved_qur_action is marked as fill). relation This field displays the name of the transNode. screenid This field displays the page ID. set_active_if Refer to Set_active_if Node Type:​ Entity: Entity defines a single entity (single row in a database table). Entity Set: An entity set is a set of entities (an entire table in a database). Query: Query which is associated with the entity. Other: Other types of transnode represent that the node is not associated with any entity. Its data can be bound from the controller. onArrive:​ Blank: If the model path is marked as blank then the data will not be set to its folded path. First: If the model path is marked as first then the first index of its entityset(folded from) will be set. History: If the model path is marked as history then it records the active index of the entityset. For example: if the model path is marked as history, then each selection of entity will be recorded. None: If the model path is marked as none then the data will not be set for that path. Set_active_if:​ Set active is classified into three categories as listed below: Always: Always defines navigation without any pre-conditions except menu navigation. Saved: Saved means navigation is permitted only if there is no dirty object in the transaction. If dirty entities are found, the Save confirmation dialog comes to ask the user if he/she wants to save the changes, otherwise, navigation is cancelled. Valid: Valid is a default value. Valid means navigation is permitted if there are no dirty objects or dirty objects are in a valid state with no error. If dirty objects are there and in an error state, the errors are highlighted on the page for the user to correct before moving forward. If the mode path’s set_active_if is provided as “valid”, on time of navigation the onValidate function (if the function is maintained in the <entity_name>.ts file) will be called. Please refer to the below matrix for all combinations of set_active_if: always saved valid Within Screen Same index of entityset(tab selection change) CREATE No Validation, No Dirty Popup No Dirty Popup No Validation Not CREATE No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Different index of entityset Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Close Detail Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Different Screen Through Manu Any Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Through Link inside screen Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation q_saved_qur_action:​ Execute: Execute will autofire the query while rendering the page. This is set as the default value. Fill: If the q_saved_qur_action is marked as true then the “q_saved_qur_id” will be filled on search. None: None means it will take no action.

documents.t: The following flags and settings control how much query/transaction detail is captured for debugging, without needing extra code. Parameter Description txn.enableStackTrace Boolean on the transaction (default false). Set true to record a stack trace of all activities of the transaction, including queries executed. Switch off again once captured. enableQueryStats Framework-internal flag (default true) driving query statistics collection. Do not disable unless instructed by platform engineering. "enableReqDump": true (klarion.json) Captures full incoming request payloads into the req_dump folder. Disabled by default. Turn off again after the investigation — req_dump folders have previously grown to multiple GB when left on. Select Distinct (Query → Detail) Set loadAll = true only when true column-level distinctness is required; otherwise leave Select Distinct off.

setPartialSelect(entityPropertyNames: string[]): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description entityPropertyNames Array of return-entity property IDs to select, instead of every property on the return entity.
setLoadAll(val: boolean): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description val Whether to load all fields of the return entity at execution time. Set false to skip properties/relations not required.
setLimit(limitValue: number): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description limitValue Maximum number of records to fetch — use for pagination on list/search screens.
setExpandAll(relations: string): string Parameter Description relations Comma-separated relation IDs to expand. Not supported together with an INNER JOIN on the same relation.

addEndpoint(endpoint, type, channel, object?, onlydirtyobject?, onlyRootEntity?): EndPointBean Parameter Description endpoint Endpoint ID(s) to notify — meaning depends on type (BP_USER, ENDPOINT, USER). type EndpointType — determines how endpoint is interpreted. channel ChannelType filter on qualifying endpoints (default DEVICE). object The KloEntity whose full BO tree is sent. Defaults to the event object. onlydirtyobject Default true — only dirty child entities are included. Set false to force all children. onlyRootEntity Default false — children already included. Set true to send the root entity alone. Note: A single addEndpoint call already messages the root entity and its (dirty) children — avoid a separate call per child entity.

documents.s: Server Side Attachment Upload — API Details

documents.t: The following BOL API methods are available on any entity property with the attachment qualifier. In server-side callbacks they are called on the property through this, for example this.attach where attach is the property name.

setAttachmentP(fileBlob, fileName): Promise<void> Parameters​ fileBlob (Blob): Blob object of the attachment to upload. fileName (string): Name of the file, including the extension. Example: report.pdf Returns​ Promise<void>: resolves once the file is uploaded to the attachment property. Description​ Uploads a file to the attachment qualifier property. It supports uploads from both server side and client side. On the server side, generate the report (PDF, CSV and so on), convert it to a Blob object and pass it to this method. Example​ const pdfBytes = await pdfDoc.save(); const blob = new Blob([pdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" }); const fileName = `order_${this.order_id || "new"}_${Date.now()}.pdf`; await this.attach.setAttachmentP(blob, fileName);

getAttachmentServerLoadP(): Promise<Uint8Array> Returns​ Promise<Uint8Array>: content of the file currently stored in the attachment property. The value is empty when no attachment exists. Description​ Loads the existing attachment from the server so that it can be read or modified in a server-side callback. To save the changes, upload the modified file again with setAttachmentP. Example​ const existingAttachment = await this.attach.getAttachmentServerLoadP(); if (!existingAttachment) { throw new Error("No attachment found to update"); } const pdfDoc = await PDFDocument.load(existingAttachment); // modify the PDF, then upload it again const modifiedBlob = new Blob([await pdfDoc.save()], { type: "application/pdf" }); await this.attach.setAttachmentP(modifiedBlob, "order_updated.pdf");

SN Steps 1 From the server side callback function, we can generate the reports[pdf, csv etc] and convert it to blob object and upload it via setAttachmentP API. Below code snippet, imports pdf-lib and generates the pdf , convert to blob object and uploads it via setAttachmentP API // Import pdf-lib for server-side PDF generation const { PDFDocument, rgb } = require("pdf-lib"); // Create a new PDF document const pdfDoc = await PDFDocument.create(); const page = pdfDoc.addPage([595, 842]); // Add content to the PDF page.drawText("ORDER DOCUMENT", { x: 50, y: 800, size: 18, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText("=".repeat(80), { x: 50, y: 780, size: 8, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Order ID: ${this.order_id || "N/A"}`, { x: 50, y: 750, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Order Description: ${this.order_desc || "N/A"}`, { x: 50, y: 730, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Created Date: ${new Date().toLocaleDateString()}`, { x: 50, y: 700, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); page.drawText(`Created Time: ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}`, { x: 50, y: 680, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); // Save the PDF to bytes const pdfBytes = await pdfDoc.save(); // Create a Blob object from PDF bytes (required by setAttachmentP) const blob = new Blob([pdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" }); // Set file name const fileName = `order_${this.order_id || "new"}_${Date.now()}.pdf`; // Upload the PDF using setAttachmentP await this.attach.setAttachmentP(blob, fileName);

documents.t: SN Steps 1 From the server side callback function, We can retrieve the previously generated PDF reports and modify them. Below code snippet, that retrieves the pdf, modified it and uploads it via setAttachmentP API // Import pdf-lib for server-side PDF modification const { PDFDocument, rgb } = require("pdf-lib"); // Load the existing attachment from server (returns Uint8Array) const existingAttachment = await this.attach.getAttachmentServerLoadP(); if (!existingAttachment) { throw new Error("No attachment found to update"); } // Load the existing PDF document directly from Uint8Array const pdfDoc = await PDFDocument.load(existingAttachment); // Get the first page (or add a new page if needed) const pages = pdfDoc.getPages(); const firstPage = pages[0]; // Add updated/modified content to the PDF firstPage.drawText("*** UPDATED ***", { x: 50, y: 650, size: 14, color: rgb(1, 0, 0), // Red color to indicate update }); firstPage.drawText(`Last Modified: ${new Date().toLocaleString()}`, { x: 50, y: 630, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 1), // Blue color }); firstPage.drawText(`Modified Order Description: ${this.order_desc || "N/A"} - MODIFIED`, { x: 50, y: 610, size: 12, color: rgb(0, 0, 0), }); // Save the modified PDF to bytes const modifiedPdfBytes = await pdfDoc.save(); // Create a Blob object from modified PDF bytes const modifiedBlob = new Blob([modifiedPdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" }); // Generate updated file name const updatedFileName = `order_${this.order_id || "new"}_updated_${Date.now()}.pdf`; // Upload the modified PDF using setAttachmentP await this.attach.setAttachmentP(modifiedBlob, updatedFileName);

When you install an app in a DEV landscape, App transport asks whether to install it As Readable or As Writable. The choice decides what is copied to the target landscape and what you can change there afterward. As Readable (Read-Only) As Writable What is moved The built application package (zip) only The app’s full metadata from the source DEV landscape Can the app be developed in the target? No Yes Can App Dependencies be maintained? No (see below) Yes Typical use Consuming an app as-is, e.g., in QA/PROD or as a parent app Continuing development in another DEV landscape Why App Dependencies can’t be maintained for a Read-Only app A Read-Only app has no metadata in the target landscape. It only has its built package. Maintaining App Dependencies writes a generated sequence to the database, and the app must be built again afterward. A Read-Only app can’t be built in the target landscape, so its dependencies can’t be changed there. Example: VP depends on OHR (VP ← OHR). If the dependency configuration has to change on the OHR side, OHR must be installed As Writable. Alternatively, make the change in the source landscape and migrate it again. Note: If you might need to change an app’s dependencies in the target landscape, install it As Writable. [Confirm] Whether a Read-Only app can be switched to Writable later, or must be reinstalled.

Transport is a tool that deploys applications from one server to another. It is mainly aimed at deploying from a dev system to QA system and from QA to PROD system but can be used across any system. Transportation of an application can be from: DEV to QA QA to PROD DEV to DEV Steps involved: DEV to QA Setup- Doing entries in tables like madm_app, madm_app_grp etc. Download- Downloading and extracting application zips from the source. Update Schema - Creating tables on the server for entities of that app. Finalizing - Making the app ACTIVE so that everyone can use it.

Maintain this configuration in target’s config file. (present in <landscape>/kloconfig/config.json) "mm_klo_online_server": { "serverUrl": "https\://dev.procify38.com", "Landscape": "tools\_dev6", "username": "transport", "password": "1", "realm": "cloud\_app" }, Where, serverUrl is the source system’s url, landscape - source System’s landscape, username - one specific user should be there with transport flavor assigned to it. password- password for that user realm - keycloak’s realm Maintain host file entry for the source system in the target system transport_1 app should be assigned to the user.

Transport takes care of the following: Maintaining entries of applications in tables like madm_app,mf_fl,mf_fv etc., if any. Moving application zips across the system (QA or PROD system) and extracting them. Getting the metadata of the application from the source DEV system and extracting it in the target DEV system. Running automated scripts if maintained. Track manual scripts and run when required. Publishing Application. Doing an updated schema on the application.

Step 5: Choose whether the app will be supported in the device, browser or both from the App/Portal Support input (default BOTH). Step 7: When you want to skip default app group creation( for Developer and Tester) then select the checkbox highlighted below during(new App/ Minor Version/Major Version) creation. Step 9: Select Auth Code (Default : COMMON) The Auth Code indicates a group of apps that manage the user/User Collections/app/App Collections for the particular app. It is a segregation process for users and apps. Below there is a Publish Settings under which we have two options: Updates Code: It will update the zip on the client side. App Data Update: It will update the client-side table data, if any. Important: There are a few things we need to know about App Versioning. The App versions are written in 6-0-1(Major-Minor-Patch). Here, 6 is referred to as Major 0 is referred to as Minor and, 1 is referred to as Patch When the patch is changed while versioning, the roles & users are automatically copied from the previous version to the recent version. If the minor or major is changed then the users will not get copied from the previous version to the new version. While creating a new version the patch number automatically changes, but when you want to create the app branch click on the branch button and it will create a branch with the latest version like major-minor+B-patch ,Note: When any new or hot fixes are made a new version should be created for that and an update should be taken for the same. All flavors within a single application hierarchy must use the same FW version to ensure compatibility and consistency. If any application in the hierarchy (that has dependencies with other flavors) requires a FW version upgrade, all associated flavors within that hierarchy must also be updated to the same new FW version. Example: If em4_6-0-1 plans to upgrade to a newer FW version (e.g., 6-1-0), then every other flavor under the same hierarchy must be versioned accordingly and updated to use 6-1-0. However, independent flavors that do not belong to this hierarchy are not required to update their FW version.

documents.t: Workspace Hub menu will be visible for Users who are assigned as TESTER or DEVELOPER or SUPERADMIN. Step 1: Go to the menu options and select Workspace Hub. Step 2: The Workspace Hub contains the following screens. Under the menu header, App Lifecycle users who are assigned as TESTER or DEVELOPER or SUPERADMIN wIll find Auth Configuration and Custom Domains menus. Under the menu header,App Lifecycle users who are assigned SUPERADMIN and not as any application role wIll find the App Authorisation menu. First, we will look into the menus under the menu header Workspace Hub. AccountDetails - For overviewing the account details of the user and modifying it. Account Name : Account Name are the basic details of the customer for which the account is created. Account Type: Account Type are the basic details of the customer for which the account is created. Valid Till: Valid till are the subscription period of the account which has been created for the customer. Valid From: Valid from are the subscription period of the account which has been created for the customer. User Management - The User screen lists the users who are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration whose accounts have been created under current landscape.We can check the details of the users, the User Collections one is assigned , the endpoints and apps assigned. Need help?: Need help is the help and support section in an Workspace Hub that includes options for contacting customer support, such as phone numbers or email details, and links to important documents like Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, and Logo sections. You can also find details on sales inquiries or account management contacts. App Management - The Apps screen lists the Apps that are created in the current landscape for which logged in user has MANAGER access . Apps help create new apps, assign users based on roles to the app, and add language and FAQ Keys. use show External checkbox to show/hide external apps (default hide). Use ShowExternal to see external apps assigned to the user as manager. User ShowAll to see all the versions of apps assigned to the user as manager. User Collections - The User Group screen lists the User Collections who are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration and have been created under the current landscape. A User Group is the section where a group of users using the same application are listed. User Collections are of two types : 1. Individual user group which is created by default for every user. By default individual User Collections are hidden, use show Individual checkbox if needed. Individual User Collections are needed to automatically assign newly created apps to the logged in user. 2. Group user group which was manually created. These groups of users can be assigned to an app group. App Collections - The App Group screen lists the App Collections which are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration and have been created under the current landscape. The App Group is used to create groups that will consist of apps which fall under a particular project or that fall under a particular user. App Collections are of two types: 1. Individual App group which is created by default during every new , major and minor App creation. By default individual App Collections are hidden, use show Individual checkbox if needed. Individual App Collections are used to assign newly created apps to the logged in user. 2. Group App group which was manually created. One can also add User Collections to the App Collections. Login Sessions - Whenever any account is registered in the application, a new endpoint ID gets created against that account. It can be checked in the endpoint section. Now, we have three menus under the menu header App Lifecycle. Let us delve in to know what each does. Auth Configuration - Here we will find the available Auth Configuration that are available in this tool and under this we can add or remove users according to our requirements. Auth Configuration are used to segregate users, apps , User Collections ,App Collections. It works as authorisation to particular users for apps, users, App Collections and User Collections. Custom Domains - Custom Domains is a URL Development for redirecting a short url to its long url version. This process is done to make the URLs convenient for the end user's understanding. Short URLs improve the user experience by being easier to type out. AI User Quota - AI User quota is a screen that will store the AI seat allocation details for the users. It consists of seat id clicking on which it will navigate to the AI conversation history screen. This screen is only visible to app admins. AI Conversation History - AI conversation history is a screen that has detailed information about the prompts and the corresponding responses that are given by user/’s using particular seats. This screen is only visible to app admins. Now, we have a menu under the menu header App Lifecycle**.** Let us delve in to know what each does. App Authorisation - In this section, the accounts of the current or existing users will be shown and the users can assign or remove apps as and when required. Note:​ After saving in the Users, User Collections and App Collections screen a popup will be shown indicating that Permission has been triggered and can be checked in the Permission Logs screen. 1.15.1.1. Business Requirement​ Application configuration wizard is to create a new application in the system by taking the necessary information, an application can also be created by taking a reference of an existing application. 1.15.1.2. Prerequisites​ All configuration tables in the system. The Application wizard and its components in the system. 1.15.1.3.Process Flow​ Path : Wizards → Application Wizard Tcode : /MVN/APP_WIZARD Report : /MVN/RP_APP_WIZARD Execute the Tcode or use Menu to open the wizard. It enters the start page of the wizard as shown below. Wizard steps​ Please read the guidelines provided in each step of the wizard carefully before proceeding with the execution of that step. Name and Integration parameters​ This step is for setting up the application configuration. Input Purpose Possible values Application-Version App and version of the newly created app. Eg:eam-1 Integration Mode Integration mode of app Online/ Offline Integration Type Integration type of app File/Gateway/PI or PO Reference From All Informations will be copied from the reference app to the newly creating app Existing App name and version Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step. Connection parameter​ This step is to provide the Connection parameters of the application. Input Purpose Possible values Gateway/PI URL URL of gateway or PI Gateway RFC Gateway RFC name Inbound folder Inbound folder path Outbound folder Outbound folder path Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step. Token parameter​ This step is to configure the token parameter of the application for the provided gateway information. Input Purpose Possible values Token URL Token url Username User name of the URL access Password Password of the URL access SSL ID SSL ID of the connection Proxy Proxy RFC: Gateway to SAP Gateway to SAP RFC Once all token parameters are provided, click the ‘TEST’ icon to verify the connection. This will display the connection status as shown below. Click on continue to move to the next step. Middleware parameter​ Modify the default middleware parameter values in this step according to the requirements, then click continue to proceed to the next page. Click the ‘Del’ icon in the table to remove parameters. Message parameter​ Edit the default message parameters in this step based on the requirement and click on continue to move on to the next page. Copy other configurations​ This step involves selecting the configurations to be copied to the new app if a reference app is available. Input Purpose Possible Values Profile determination To copy the profile determination configurations BO Handler To copy the BO Handler configurations Klo Model To copy the Klo Model configurations F4 Mappings To copy the F4 Mappings configurations Select the checkbox if the specified configurations should be copied. This applies only if a reference app is provided in the Name and Integration parameters section. Wizard Finish​ Review the provided details in the wizard summary and click the Complete button to finalize the application creation. 1.15.1.4. Wizard Results​ An application is created with the provided details as below, Connection Parameters:​ Path: Klobase Configuration cockpit -> Application configuration -> Application Configuration T-code : /MVN/KB_VC_APP_CONF Middleware Parameters:​ Path: Klobase Configuration cockpit -> Application configuration -> Application Configuration T-code : /MVN/KB_VC_APP_CONF Message Parameters​ Path: Klobase Configuration cockpit -> Application configuration -> Application Configuration T-code : /MVN/KB_VC_APP_CONF Other Configurations​ If the reference app is provided, the Properties selected in the ‘’Copy Other configuration’’ sections such as Profile Determination, Bo Handler, Klo model and F4 mapping will be copied.

This tile allows the user to edit fields such as app admin flavor, registration flavor, registration flavor version, app admin flavor version, notification template, notification type, notification duration and notification count. Description for the above fields are as follows: Fields Description Registration Flavor We have to mention what is the registration flavor here in this column. For ATL they require customization, so they have different names. (If you require some changes to be done in the flavor maintain that flavor name here.) Notification Duration If we are sending an OTP, it should be valid for a few minutes before it expires. Notification Count If the OTP is not received by the user, the number of times the user is allowed to click on resend the OTP. After the maximum attempts are over, the user is blocked in the keycloak.

kloBroker is a broker between tenants, clients, and external systems. It enables communication via messaging and queues. kloBroker runs on the master node in the kloSystem. There can be multiple instances, one per kloLandscape. This dialog allows the user to modify klobroker fields such as mw_msg_pick, mw required, notif required, bol enabled, fcm server key, base path, external file size, holding time, notif interval, notif threshold, interval, queue size, threshold, queue creation class, max message per file, SQL batch size, notif pick size and file parallel count. This dialog also allows CRUD on klobroker external fields which contain endpointid, type, destination host, destination port, destination protocol, user ID, password, and destination path. Description for the above fields are as follows: Fields Description MW Msg Pick This implies the number of messages middleware can pick from the tenant_q table. MW Required This implies whether middleware is required or not. Notif Required Server will send push notifications to the device. It will push all notifications to one table(ma_notification_queue). FCM Server Key To sync the message from the server to the device, fcm_server_key is mandatory. Base Path SAP will put files in this folder and the server will pick files. External File Size Size of the external files Notif Interval It will check in the queue at intervals whether the messages are present or not. Notif threshold The Maximum number of notifications the server will pick. Interval For how much time the DB needs to be checked, the Server will check whether the file is available or not in the sap in the folder and if the file is available then it will process or it will not. Threshold The number of messages the server will hold at a time. Notif pick size The number of notifications it can pick at a time

This will only consider SAP_LOCAL or SAP_ONLINE. It will not consider if it has any extra symbols or any extensions like SAP_LOCAL_ or SAP_LOCAL. Description for the above fields are as follows: Fields Description SAP_LOCAL If something is being saved in the DB, then it will go to tenant_q and save in the klarion db, then we need to push to SAP as a JSON message. SAP_ONLINE When we are directly accessing the SAP server without saving in our db, in this case, we use SAP_ONLINE. TYPE Destination Host Here we are maintaining the url provided by SAP. User Id User Id provided by SAP for the url. Password Password provided by SAP for the url. Destination Path When the type is a folder, then we specify a path here. Note :​ File processing. When processing SAP messages by file, txn_user_id has to be maintained in KloBroker configuration, or else, the generated messages will go to error q without user in transaction. The user ID maintained should have required application, row wise authorization(If required), permissions assigned.
